LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. The Panthers won the NFC South last season, but a litany of injuries to open the 2026 campaign have put them in a tough spot to repeat. It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. That being said, Carolina is missing some big guns on defense, including their star pass rusher. Even if Matthew Golden cannot go or is on limited reps, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft should be able to make enough plays in the passing game. Perhaps Josh Jacobs can finally find some room to roam on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Expect a sloppy game, but the Packers will make one more play than the Panthers, getting them to 5-3 before a much-needed mini bye week. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 17, Panthers 14. away.blurb: So can the Panthers sustain their recent success? Will Mayfield’s return yield a new hope? Will the NFC South standings be shaken up? Fans can also check the game out on radio: WRFX The Fox, 99.7 FM. Anish Shroff (play-by-play), Luke Kuechly (analyst), Jake Delhomme (analyst), Jim Szoke (host), Kristen Balboni (sideline). For full local listings, check out the Carolina Panthers Radio Network . Special note: Kuechly will receive his Pro Football Hall of Fame ring at halftime of the game in Bank of America Stadium. Out: OLB Thomas Incoom (calf), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) Questionable: OT Monroe Freeling (knee), LB Bam Martin-Scott (hamstring) Out: WR Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), OT Luke Goedeke (calf), S Antoine Winfield (rib) Questionable: QB Baker Mayfield (right thumb) Alex Zietlow: Panthers 35, Bucs 31. I know that Baker Mayfield’s almost-certain return will make this Bucs offense more dynamic. And I know that scoring 35 on this Bucs team will be difficult, considering their opportunistic defensive backfield and their Top 5 rush defense. Still, barring an implosion of turnovers, I think the Panthers outscore and outlast a Bucs team trying to get back on track. Can the Carolina Panthers make it three wins in a row? And can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers get back on track? The Panthers (3-2) are returning to Bank of America Stadium for their Week 7 contest (1 p.m., FOX) fresh off two statement victories against the Detroit Lions and the Philadelphia Eagles . They’re looking to go 4-2 for the first time as a franchise since 2019 and start 2-0 in the NFC South for the first time since 2022. Carolina ranks first in the NFL in passing yards per game (295.6), second in total yards per game (404.4) and fourth in points per game (29.2). And its defense — minus the Week 1 fiasco against the Bears that’s looking more and more like an aberration — is Top 10 in several statistics, including rushing yards allowed. The Panthers have allowed fewer than 50 yards in each of the last two weeks: 46 against the Lions, 35 against the Eagles. It’s true that the defense is a bit affected by injury, specifically at the outside linebacker spot with no Jaelan Phillips or Thomas Incoom this week . It’s also true that the defense has only had to play against starting quarterbacks three times so far this season, and two of those three — against Caleb Williams of the Bears and Deshaun Watson of the Browns — have yielded losses. That won’t happen this week; it looks like the Bucs will be led by Baker Mayfield, who’s missed the last few weeks with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand. Speaking of the Bucs (1-5): While many of their offensive stats might be skewed by Mayfield’s absence, many of their strengths will remain. Namely? Their rush defense. Tampa Bay ranks second in the NFL in rush yards allowed per game at 75.5, thanks to a defensive line anchored by nose tackle Vita Vea and an entire unit led by rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter. away.headline: Panthers' concerns going into Thursday's game against the Packers just got even worse based on the final Week 8 injury report
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers had a lot of concerns going into this week after the beatdown the team suffered on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. To make things even harder, the Panthers had a short turnaround to make adjustments with a road trip coming up on Thursday against the Green Bay Packers. That already was going to be a rough road matchup for this team with everything going on coming out of the last game, and to make things even worse, the team's final Week 8 injury report added even more concerns. First off, the Panthers have officially ruled out star pass rusher Jaelan Phillips for the second consecutive game with a hamstring injury. Given the nature of the injury, the fact it's a reaggravation, and this being a short week, it was always unlikely that Phillips would have been able to play against the Packers. Wednesday's injury report confirmed those suspicions, leaving the Panthers without their top edge rusher. Being without Phillips really hurt the Panthers last week. Tampa Bay exposed the Panthers in the run game attacking the edges with counters and rumbled for over 250 yards on the ground. It was an embarrassing performance and not having Phillips out there to set the edge was a big reason for it, along with poor tackling. Big picture, sitting Phillips is the right call for him. He needs to get that hamstring figured out before rushing back into action like he did in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles, which is what caused this injury to reaggravate in the first place. The Panthers need Phillips for the long haul and need him fully healthy before returning. Another notable injury designation is left guard Damien Lewis, who will be out for Thursday's game due to a knee injury. Lewis was easily the team's best offensive lineman, allowing seven pressures this season on over 200 pass blocking snaps. The other four starters have each allowed 15+ pressures this season. The Panthers are also without backup guard Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) and elevated Jake Curhan from the practice squad as a result. The Panthers also placed veteran right tackle Taylor Moton on the injured reserve earlier this week after he fractured his fibula along with further damage to his ankle. That leaves Monroe Freeling to fill back in at right tackle, which in turn forces Rasheed Walker to remain at left tackle. Those two have allowed a combined five sacks and 42 pressures. In Lewis place at left guard, the Panthers will likely turn to Corey Bullock, who's played 71 pass blocking snaps this season with one sack and five pressures allowed. It's a tough look for quarterback Bryce Young, who has been having to overcome pressure all season long. One more worrisome injury to note is in the secondary. Akayleb Evans will not play either due to a triceps/knee injury. Evans has been filling in as a starter, and largely has struggled, in place of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. away.headline: Panthers place Akayleb Evans on injured reserve, among other moves
away.blurb: The Panthers placed cornerback Akayleb Evans on injured reserve. He was already ruled out this week because of knee and triceps injuries. He had started the last three games, after the Panthers placed both Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson on injured reserve following Week 3. The veteran corner and special teamer will now be out for at least the next four games. Week 8 Wednesday Injury Report: Four ruled out for Packers game To replace him on the 53-man roster, they signed cornerback Malcolm DeWalt IV , who was just signed last week and arrived Sunday. He had been on the Falcons' 53-man roster, but was a healthy scratch in all six games he was there. The undrafted rookie from Akron (among other places) stood out in the preseason for the Falcons, earning a roster spot with his ability on defense and special teams. Guards Damien Lewis and Torricelli Simpkins III are out this week with injuries, and they were down to Will Lee III and Chau Smith-Wade at cornerback this week. A 27-19 loss to the Packers was one thing, but the Panthers lost yet another cornerback, as rookie Will Lee III was carted off with a hamstring injury and did not return. Bobby Brown is inactive for Thursday's game, after being listed as questionable on the final injury report of the week. He was initially listed as questionable to return but ultimately remained out for the rest of the game. When Will Jonathon Brooks Return? The initial recovery estimate provides the clearest indication of Brooks' potential return. Panthers head coach Dave Canales said the running back was expected to miss six to eight weeks following surgery. That projected recovery timeline offers hope that Brooks could return sometime in November, though the Panthers have not confirmed a specific date for his comeback. The Panthers have not announced an official return date for the running back. His progress toward full participation in practice will be crucial in determining when he can rejoin the lineup. The Carolina Panthers are preparing to take on the Green Bay Packers on Thursday Night Football in Week 8. However, Carolina will once again be without running back Jonathon Brooks. After battling a series of injuries dating back to his college days, Brooks has continued to face injury setbacks in his professional career. The Panthers' running back has appeared in just two games so far this season and is currently on injured reserve after suffering an injury during Carolina's Week 2 win over the Atlanta Falcons. What Happened to Jonathon Brooks? Brooks will miss Thursday's game as he continues recovering from a core muscle injury that required surgery. He re-aggravated a lingering groin injury against Atlanta, with the issue later diagnosed as a core muscle injury that required surgery. Carolina selected Brooks in the second round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Unfortunately, injuries have continued to interrupt his development. For The Latest Information: NFL Injury Report Brooks missed most of his rookie season while recovering from a torn ACL. After appearing in just three games as a rookie, he re-injured the knee and required another procedure, forcing him to miss the entire 2025 season. Earlier in the year, while still working his way back from a second ACL tear, Brooks reflected on the difficulty of the rehabilitation process and his hope of returning to the field. "I mean, obviously it's like an emotional roller coaster, but you know, truthfully, I know that God has a plan for me and I know that he makes no mistakes and he's using my story to show the world the amazing things he can do, and so I'm set on that," Brooks said

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. His activation makes him eligible to play against Buffalo and adds depth to a secondary preparing to face Josh Allen and the NFL's highest-scoring offense. Ioane suffered an MCL sprain during Baltimore's 35-13 loss to Cincinnati and returned to practice Thursday and Friday, but the rookie will miss Sunday's contest. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Bengals in Week 8, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Heading into Week, the 1-6 Tennessee Titans have everything to prove, but also nothing at all. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. I was already wary of the Tennessee Titans' motivations heading into their Week 8 road date with the Cincinnati Bengals. Then Tennessee traded All-Pro DT Jeffery Simmons to Chicago Thursday afternoon. That move tacked on an extra point to this surging spread, with Cincinnati now laying -11.5 on Sunday afternoon. My Titans vs. Bengals predictions size up that mountain of chalk as well as the crater Simmons leaves in this Tennessee stop unit. Here are my best NFL picks for Nov. 1. TOP Pick Titans vs Bengals prediction: Over 46.5 One of my first plays of Week 8 was taking the Over in this game. And with Jeffery Simmons swapping out his trademark red sleeves for Chicago orange, I like the Over even more considering the Cincinnati Bengals will do the heavy lifting. Simmons was the shining star and identity of the Tennessee Titans defense. His absence up front will drop the Titans even further down the defensive pecking order, which says something when they're already dead last in DVOA at FTN . The Bengals picked apart a very good Baltimore stop unit in the second half of Sunday's win. They finished with 7.0 yards per play and were a perfect 5 for 5 in the red zone, with Joe Burrow and his talented receiving corps finding their stride. Tennessee's secondary allows the second-highest completion rate and has been burned by multiple big plays, bleeding the fourth most passes of 20+ yards entering Week 8. While the Titans haven't given up many passing touchdowns, they haven't played many QBs on Burrow's level. Titans vs Bengals combo The Bengals do the lion's share of the scoring but don't discount the Titans. Tennessee is playing with pace and faces a Cincy defense that still has work to do. Chase Brown finds the end zone to the cheers of fantasy owners everywhere. He faces a watered-down Titans defense that's allowed six scores to running backs. Tee Higgins' projections call for as many as 91 yards against a Tennessee secondary giving up explosive plays. Chase Brown touchdown Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Titans vs Bengals touchdown scorer: Chase Brown If anyone was happy to see Simmons traded before Week 8, it was Bengals running back Chase Brown. He no longer has to worry about one of the premier run stoppers in the game, facing a Tennessee red-zone defense now missing its biggest cog. Even when Simmons was in the mix, Tennessee had allowed six scores to rival RBs. Brown has only one touchdown in 2026 despite 13 carries and three receptions in the red zone. Due to that drought, we're getting a discount on his ATTD market in Week 8 considering this prop was trading around 60% two games ago. Given the massive spread, Cincinnati will be in a run-positive game script in the second half of Sunday, helping boost Brown's TD probabilities. His TD forecasts range between 60% and 78%, given he's a threat to run one in or catch a touchdown pass. Titans vs Bengals player prop: Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Cincinnati has arguably the best one-two punch at receiver in the NFL, with Tee Higgins serving as "Robin" to Ja'Marr Chase's "Batman". But don't tell Higgins that. He looked more like Superman in Week 7, putting in a monster effort in the win over the rival Ravens. He caught six of seven balls his way for 148 yards and a touchdown. That includes a 44-yard dinger on a broken play with Burrow dodging pressure. We mentioned the Titans' problems giving up home runs over the top, and Higgins is one of the best deep threats in the land, averaging 21.6 air yards per reception and amassing eight catches for 20+ yards. Tennessee has also been burned by WR2s to start the season, rating 24th in DVOA vs. WR2s at FTN while giving up almost 56 yards per game to those second options. Higgins' Week 8 models are very bullish on his receiving yards, ranging from 65 to a high of 91. Most forecasts come in above 80 yards, and my projection sits just shy of 81 yards receiving. home.headline: Ja'Marr Chase's absence from Bengals practice gets an explanation in latest injury report
home.blurb: Chase (ankle) officially had a rest day, but is also listed with an ankle injury. He was seen in the locker room after practice. The "rest" being listed as the primary reason for his DNP insinuates it is not a serious injury, but seeing what the rest of his week looks like will be key before Sunday's game. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during last Sunday's win over the Baltimore Ravens and is back to being "week-to-week." Coach Zac Taylor has already declared Dugger out for this week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen got his usual rest day. S Jordan Battle was limited with a hamstring injury, which he's been playing through for the last month. Linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) was also limited. Four Titans did not practice due to injuries including their first-round pick, WR Carnell Tate (shoulder). Tate has played in all seven games for Tennessee this season, catching 34 passes for 413 yards and a touchdown. Fellow receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) went limited. He's been dealing with his hip injury for the last week and missed last Sunday's game because of it. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) was also a DNP. He's been playing next to All-Pro Jeffery Simmons and has produced 13 pressures and 1.5 sacks in seven games. Backup running back Tyjae Spears (knee) and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) were also non-participants Wednesday in Nashville. Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers (groin/back) is questionable. Tennessee is fighting depth up front after trading Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears . The Titans signed Timmy Horne from the practice squad and claimed former Raiders defensive tackle Jonah Laulu off waivers this week. Hill (Rest), DNP/No designation DT Dexter Lawrence II (Rest), DNP/no designation Punter Tommy Townsend also missed practice with a knee injury, prompting the team to sign Thomas Morstead. Tennessee Titans rookie and leading receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals , according to the team's Oct. 30 injury report. Tate has a team-high 34 catches for 413 yards and a touchdown this season. He has not practiced all week. Titans running back and leading rusher Tony Pollard (rest) was a full participant on Oct. 30 and has no injury designation. Pollard, who has been the talk of trade rumors, has rushed for 478 yards and four touchdowns in seven games. Backup running back Tyjae Spears (knee) will not play against the Bengals. picks.blurb: Cardinals vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Cardinals vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:20 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Arizona Cardinals are staying the course with quarterback Jacboy Brissett. Meanwhile, at least one person thinks the Dallas Cowboys don't need trade deadline help. These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. The Cowboys are 3-4, but they play in a woefully weak NFC East. They're still favored to win the division. It's a far different world for the Cardinals, who stand at 2-5 and are buried in last place in one of the NFL's toughest divisions, the NFC West. Let's take a look at what to expect. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cowboys QB Dak Prescott will throw 3 TD passes again Prescott didn't have to do much against the Eagles as the Cowboys ran the ball at will. But he still had three touchdown throws. This will be more of the same, with a lot of runs and Prescott finishing off drives with TD passes. No matter what Stephen A. Smith says, Prescott is still that dude. Of course, it seems like Smith will say anything to keep his show in the spotlight. He questioned whether the Cowboys still have confidence in Prescott on First Take via Sports Illustrated. "This is my interpretation," Smith said. "I believe there's a lack of confidence, supreme confidence in Dak Prescott. You believe in him, you're paying him, but in the same breath, you're understanding the importance of having that balanced running attack. Because when you just have him dropping back the pass that football, you're not satisfied with the level of production that you're getting." Whatever. The only way Prescott might not have a big game is if the Cardinals' defense gets gashed for 5-, 10-, and 20-yard TD runs. Oh, well, that is possible. The Cardinals have a rotten defense. Cowboys WR George Pickens will catch multiple TD passes Here's the trick: Prescott will be able to pick and choose who he wants to get the TD catches. And since Lamb has already been well established with six TD receptions in 2026, look for Prescott to make sure Pickens, who has two, closes the gap. With 16 fewer catches than Lamb on the season, it's not a stretch to see Pickens get double-digit grabs in this contest. Now, Pickens is banged up, but it's probably one of those mid-week no-biggies. The injuries are to his shoulder and hamstring, according to NBC Sports. "Pickens played through a minor shoulder injury last week, but the hamstring designation is new," Aditya Fuldeore wrote. "He was still a limited practice participant, indicating neither injury should be an issue for his Week 8 status." Both receivers are supremely confident , as Lamb expressed, according to dallasnews.com. "I think that's pretty self-explanatory, to be honest," Lamb said. "Once we get going, I don't think there's … nah, I know for a fact, there's not a person in this league that can stop us." And Pickens said he's learning patience. "It's just super important just because that can boost the morale of the team when you just wait your turn," Pickens said. "Whether you're a running back, tight end, you make your play that boosts the offense." Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will throw for 280-plus yards It has been an up-and-down season for the veteran quarterback. But this is a game where volume will lead to yardage, even if it is in a game that winds up with a no-so-close loss. Brissett seems to be on the verge of losing his starting job. So look for him to be focused and effective at times. Head coach Mike LaFleur said the offensive issues aren't all on Brissett, according to NBC Sports. "Like I told you guys, he's still the starter," LaFleur said, via transcript from the team. "It's collective. Again, if the ball was just stagnant for 60 minutes and you couldn't even cross the 50-yard line, it'd be one thing. We've been down inside the 10-yard line 10 times over the last two games, so the ball is moving, but we have to finish jobs. Again, that starts with me, but that's a collective effort. "The players have to go execute. And I have to put them in better positions and give them the clarity to go do so. When they do have that clarity, they have to make the plays. We know that. We're not going to shy away from that. We know we have to finish the job when we're down there, and I don't even think we're having these conversations right now [if we had]." away.headline: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 8 Status Revealed
away.blurb: Jeremiyah Love has battled an ankle injury throughout the season, but he could make his long-awaited return to the field in Week 8. The Arizona Cardinals gave him the most guaranteed money of any running back in NFL history when they selected him with the third-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and it's easy to see why. The Notre Dame product dominated at the collegiate level, routinely flashing his elite athleticism and ability to make plays both as a runner and a returner. In theory, he has the talent to be a true three-down workhorse like Atlanta's Bijan Robinson and Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs . Unfortunately for everyone involved, Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during his first real taste of NFL action. The running back suffered an ankle injury midway through the contest and missed most of the preseason. While he has played in five games despite the injury, he did not play in Week 7. While nobody knows for sure if he will play in Week 8, the team's official practice report notes the running back returned to the field in a limited capacity, which bodes well for this week. So far, the running back has recorded just 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 attempts, good for just 3.7 yards per carry. While the Cardinals passing attack and subpar offensive line certainly haven't done anything to ease the pressure on the rookie, he hasn't looked like his college self either. Hopefully, taking some time to rest will help him recapture his collegiate form. In his absence, free agent signee Tyler Allgeier has not done much to impress. Despite his lofty contract, veteran Zonavan Knight has looked like the better player and will almost certainly earn the start if Jeremiyah Love cannot play. Main Photo: David Brytus – Imagn Images

home.headline: Cowboys Activate Defensive Reinforcement Off IR Among 2 Roster Moves Before Week 8 Game
home.blurb: Locke is one of two Cowboys safeties to land on injured reserve this season, along with Jalen Thompson, who has yet to be designated to return as he deals with a hamstring issue. Schoonmaker was added on Thursday and did not practice over the last two days of the week before drawing a questionable tag. Based on the elevation of Mitchell, it's a good bet that Schoonmaker won't suit up on Sunday. The Dallas Cowboys have made a few roster moves ahead of their Week 8 game against the Arizona Cardinals. The team announced it has activated safety P.J. Locke off injured reserve, which gives Dallas' struggling defense a much-needed reinforcement for Sunday afternoon. In addition to that move, the Cowboys have elevated tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad. One of the team's offseason free-agent signings , Locke has not appeared in a game since Week 2 after suffering a foot injury in that contest that forced his placement on injured reserve. Thompson was placed on injured reserve after Week 3 and was initially expected to miss four to six weeks. He is now four weeks into that timeline, so he could be back in the next few. With Locke back, he should slot into a starting role next to Malik Hooker, which will push Alijah Clark and Markquese Bell down on the depth chart. However, don't be surprised if Clark still sees a good amount of playing time, as he has shined for Dallas in the absences of Locke and Thompson. Th elevation of Mitchell comes amid uncertainty surrounding tight end Luke Schoonmaker, who popped up on the injury report this week with a groin issue. A former fifth-round pick of the Detroit Lions, Mitchell was signed to the Cowboys' practice squad in early September after cutdown day. Assuming he plays on Sunday, this will be his first game action of 2026. Mitchell has appeared in 35 games (one start) over four seasons in the NFL and has recorded 16 catches for 169 yards. His best year was his rookie season in 2022, when Mitchell reeled in 11 receptions for 113 yards. Mitchell hasn't proven to be a reliable blocker during his four-year career, but he does have the ability to make a dent in the passing game if called upon. We'll know for sure if Schoonmaker or Mitchell will be active when the Cowboys drop their inactives at around 11:30 a.m. ET on Sunday morning. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday. It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Dakota Allen Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North is officially the most explosive division in football, and Ford Field will serve as ground zero this Sunday. The 4-2 Detroit Lions are fresh off a thrilling, last-second 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers. They are set to host the league's final remaining undefeated juggernaut: the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings. This Week eight clash is a textbook battle of strengths. Head coach Dan Campbell has Jared Goff playing at an early-season MVP level, engineering an electric offense. Meanwhile, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is piloting a historic, blitz-heavy defensive unit that is suffocating opposing quarterbacks. With massive divisional implications on the line, here are three bold predictions for this highly anticipated rivalry game. 1. Jared Goff Extends Interception-Free Streak to 7 Games Despite Massive Blitz Brian Flores' defense leads the NFL in blitz percentage (38%) and thrives on turning ordinary passing downs into an absolute nightmare. The Vikings' defense has already forced 11 takeaways and racked up 21 sacks. Statistically, Flores loves to force opposing quarterbacks into hurried mistakes. The first bold prediction is that Jared Goff will throw for over 275 yards, multiple touchdowns, and maintain a completely clean sheet with zero turnovers. Goff is currently on an unbelievable heater, throwing 14 touchdowns to zero interceptions through six games. While Flores will throw a kitchen sink of disguised coverages and loaded fronts at him, Goff boasts a stellar 127.1 passer rating against the blitz this season. Shielded by one of the best offensive lines in football, Goff will stay calm in the pocket, pick apart the blitz, and keep the football safe. 2. Jahmyr Gibbs Cracks 120+ Rushing Yards The Vikings have given up very little through the air, ranking near the top of the league in passing defense. However, if their elite unit has a minor vulnerability, it is on the ground. Last week, the Indianapolis Colts exposed some cracks by carving up Minnesota for 154 rushing yards. The second bold prediction is that Jahmyr Gibbs will erupt for over 120 rushing yards and a touchdown. Gibbs has been an absolute workhorse for Detroit, averaging an astounding 103.3 rushing yards per game. Though Flores historically found success neutralizing Gibbs last season, Drew Petzing's offensive scheme will counter Minnesota's aggressive defensive stunts by leaning heavily on the ground game. Gibbs will tire out the Vikings' pass-rushers, hit the secondary at full speed, and log his biggest performance of the year. 3. Lions Hand the Vikings Their First Loss of the Season Minnesota's 6-0 start has been heavily reliant on their elite defense. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. away.headline: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return)
away.blurb: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return) Skip to main content SI.COM Minnesota moved to 6-0 after getting past the listless Colts, and also came out of the game relatively healthy as an added bonus. A few Vikings did leave the game with injury, though, so there are a few names to watch this week ahead of a date with the Detroit Lions. Vikings who could return in Week 8 Price took a big hit on a punt return and was evaluated for a concussion. He was cleared to return to the game, but head coach Kevin O'Connell did say that Price was dealing with a stinger after the win. It didn't seem to affect the star returner, and there shouldn't be much concern heading into Week 8. Still, Price is one of those players that is darn-near irreplaceable for the Vikings if he did have to miss time. The Vikings' first-round pick exited the game with an apparent lower-body injury. And while his name didn't come up postgame as a possible serious injury, Banks' two previous foot injuries that forced him out of football for almost a year are certainly at the forefront of fans' minds. Banks didn't return after limping off the field , and his status will be something to monitor throughout the week. Luckily, the Vikings didn't appear to lose anyone to a long-term injury on Sunday. The key Vikings out for the season remained the same with Donovan Jackson, Josh Oliver, Jamal Adams and Tyler Batty all already lost for the year. With various injuries on offense, defense and even one on special teams, here's who should be fine, and who might miss some time for Minnesota. Like Price, Addison was evaluated for a concussion before being cleared to play shortly after. Still, he wasn't able to do much in the contest, notching just two catches for 20 yards. Addison had already missed the Week 5 contest with a hamstring issue, but it appears he should have a clean bill of health to try and right the ship heading into the Lions matchup. Jones has been battling a knee injury all season, and once again aggravated it late in the game against the Colts. O'Connell called the injury day-to-day after the game, but it wouldn't be too surprising if Jones needs a week off to let things heal. The Vikings have ridden Jones hard this season with Jordan Mason's own injury issues, and the toll on his body is adding up quickly. If Jones can't shake this nagging knee issue, the Vikings could look to make a move for another runner at the trade deadline . Still, Jones has given his all this season, and it's hard to see him voluntarily coming off the field. Obviously injury concerns have been a big talking point with Banks, and if he does have to miss time, fellow rookie Domonique Orange could get some more run . picks.headline: Jets vs. Raiders: 5 bold predictions for Week 8
picks.blurb: Jets vs. Raiders: 5 bold predictions for Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Jets vs. Raiders: 5 bold predictions for Week 8 Geoffrey A Knox, Jets Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 12:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets are running out of opportunities to turn their season around, and Sunday's matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders presents a chance to stop the bleeding. At 2-5, Aaron Glenn's team has lost two straight games, including a frustrating divisional defeat against the previously winless Miami Dolphins . Another setback would make an already disappointing season considerably more difficult to salvage. Fortunately for New York, the Raiders aren't exactly arriving in peak condition. Las Vegas has dropped four consecutive games after opening the season 3-0, and its recent offensive struggles have created some questions of its own. Neither team can afford another afternoon of wasted opportunities, making this an interesting matchup between two teams looking to rediscover their footing. There are reasons to believe the Jets can finally put together a complete performance at MetLife Stadium. Here are five bold predictions for Week 8. Geno Smith and Garrett Wilson connect for 100-plus receiving yards and a touchdown Garrett Wilson, Jets fans, and plenty of people covering the team will be happy campers after this one. Wilson has too often been an afterthought in an offense that needs its best playmakers involved, and Sunday presents an opportunity to change that narrative. Smith and Wilson connect for more than 100 receiving yards, with the star wideout finding the end zone. After all the discussion about getting Wilson more opportunities, the Jets finally make that connection a central part of their offensive production. Ashton Jeanty finishes with fewer than 65 rushing yards Ashton Jeanty ran for 102 yards in the Raiders ' season opener, but he hasn't come close to that production since. He hasn't exceeded 58 rushing yards in any subsequent game, and his highest rushing total over Las Vegas' last three outings was just 27 yards. Now he faces a Jets defense that he decided to publicly criticize before the game. Jeanty questioned whether some New York defenders actually want to tackle, so the motivation factor shouldn't be difficult to find. The Jets respond by limiting him to 65 yards or fewer, making the Raiders running back work for everything he gets. The Jets intercept Kirk Cousins Cousins threw three interceptions combined during the first two weeks of the season before posting a clean outing in Week 3. Since then, he's developed an alternating pattern of games with an interception and games without one. He avoided a turnover against Kansas City in Week 7, which puts him in line for another costly mistake. The Jets' defense has playmakers capable of taking advantage when opposing quarterbacks become careless. Cousins has already demonstrated that he can put the football in harm's way, and New York breaks up his turnover-free streak by coming away with an interception. New York rushes for 150 yards and a touchdown The Jets enter Week 8 averaging 96.4 rushing yards per game, while Las Vegas has surrendered 143.6 yards per contest. That is a substantial difference in production, and New York has an opportunity to take advantage of a defense that has struggled to contain opposing ground attacks. The prediction calls for 150 rushing yards and at least one touchdown. Establishing the run would also help take pressure off Smith, give the offense some balance and make the Raiders defend the entire field rather than simply anticipating another passing attempt. The Jets win a back-and-forth affair New York has scored at least 23 points in three games this season. In its other four outings, the offense has failed to reach 19 points, making consistency a significant concern heading into Sunday. The Raiders need this victory just as badly, having lost four straight, so neither team should lack motivation. This one turns into a back-and-forth affair, with both offenses finding enough production to keep the outcome in doubt late. Ultimately, the Jets make a few more plays when it matters and escape with a much-needed victory. Prediction: Jets 27, Raiders 24. home.blurb: Las Vegas appears to be getting healthier after several players participated in Wednesday's practice on a limited basis: Kwity Paye, DJ Glaze, Brock Bowers, Folorunso Fatukasi, Ian Thomas, and Quay Walker. Patrick Johnson did not participate in Wednesday's practice. On Friday, Jack Bech was added to the injury report, despite practicing every day this week. He is listed as questionable for Sunday's game. Johnson was ruled out for Sunday's game, as was Runyon. Veteran cornerback Eric Stokes was added to the report with an illness on Friday after not appearing on the injury report at all this week. Stokes participated on a limited basis in Friday's practice. Stokes is Las Vegas' best cornerback. Stokes' illness could negatively impact an already questionable group of defensive backs. Beyond Stokes' illness, Las Vegas also has unanswered questions elsewhere in its defensive backfield, as it tries to decide who the best option is to play alongside Stokes: Hezekiah Masses or Darien Porter. According to Kubiak, Powers-Johnson is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets. Las Vegas needs help at the guard position but also has to consider moves that could make them better moving forward as the trade deadline approaches. On the other hand, a young offensive lineman with undeniable upside could entice another team. If Las Vegas could get even a mid-to-late-round pick in return, they should consider making the trade. The potential trade market for Powers-Johnson is worth the Raiders kicking the tires on.
