The Browns are no easy challenge this time around, and the Steelers learned that firsthand several weeks ago. The Browns won their first meeting on Thursday Night Football, but the matchup shifts to Acrisure Stadium for Week 8, and the Steelers intend to exact some revenge on their divisional foes. Both squads enter with a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. It’s a measuring-stick showdown between the Steelers and Browns, and bold actions will be taken. Both Teams Score 25 Points or More Both of these franchises bring strong defenses to their Week 8 contest. The Steelers rank in the top 10 in total yards allowed per game, rushing yards allowed per game and points allowed per contest. They also rank 11th in passing yards allowed per game. Similarly, the Browns rank in the top 15 across multiple defensive categories. It’s going to be a matchup of two stout defensive units, right? Well what would be more surprising than these two teams putting up an offensive showdown? That’s what could be in store for these two teams, despite all signs pointing toward the opposite. The Steelers rank 22nd in the NFL in points per game, posting an average of 21.9. The Browns trail, recording the 28th-best average of 19.0 points per game. But, the Steelers have also reached the 24-point mark four times in seven tries, and they could put up even more in Week 8. Oct 11, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard (17) carries the ball in the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers If the Steelers are going to buck the trend and put up points, there are two approaches to help accomplish that. One is to exploit their 19th-ranked run defense, which has to be at the top of their game plan as Jaylen Warren continues to put up MVP-caliber production. Another avenue, the more unexpected one for the offense to take, is to push the ball downfield with the passing game. In the team’s first matchup against the Browns, Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf posted five receptions on nine targets for 115 yards. And they managed to break off his biggest play of the game by getting him away from Cleveland’s top defender, Denzel Ward. If the Steelers can capture that again in Week 8, quarterback Aaron Rodgers could have a magical day. In 2025, Rodgers never hit the 300-yard mark. His 2026 season high so far is 299 yards, which he threw for during that previous contest against the Browns. In the three weeks since, he hasn’t surpassed 255 yards, but this could be the one where he eclipses 300 yards. Germie 100-Yard Game Incoming If Rodgers is throwing that many yards, one of his receivers has to have an outstanding day on the stat sheet. After he earned more and more trust, Bernard could face a favorable matchup if he doesn’t go against Ward too often. He’s gotten close, putting up two 80+ yard games so far this season. This week, it finally happens. The second-round pick eclipses 100 yards for the first time in his young NFL career. The Steelers are looking for payback and the Browns are looking for their first sweep of the Steelers since 1988. Here are four bold predictions for this week's game. Jaylen Warren carries the offense The Browns run defense is struggling and Jaylen Warren is on a tear. Warren rushed for 93 yards in the first matchup and our bold prediction for Warren this week is he gets his fourth 100-yard rushing game of the year and tops 150 yards of total offense and two total touchdowns. T.J. Watt breaks out with 3 sacks This week is the perfect opportunity for T.J. Watt to quiet the critics as he faces backup right tackle Dawand Jones. Watt is currently fourth int he NFL with 5.5 sacks but has struggled with consistent pressure. This week he breaks out of his funk with a huge three-sack performance and one of them turns into a huge forced fumble. Pittsburgh solves their red zone woes with two scores For all the things he can do, head coach Mike McCarthy has struggled to get the Steelers red-zone offense on track. This is due in large part because he's been unwilling to just run the football near the goal line. That ends this week with two short rushing touchdowns. The Steelers currently have only one rushing touchdown all season. Double-digit win for the Steelers We appreciate what the Browns are building but Pittsburgh is at home and riding a three-game win streak since the loss to Cleveland and will keep it going with a double-digit win, bringing the Browns back to Earth about their place in the AFC North. picks.headline: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jarrett Bailey Sat, October 31, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads First place in the AFC North is up for grabs as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. Both teams enter the day at 5-2, with Cleveland holding a 1-0 head-to-head advantage over Pittsburgh. Will they beat the Steelers on the road in a regular season game for the first time since 2003? Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns twice in a season in almost three decades, but this year presents a unique challenge. Teams traveling internationally over the last two seasons are just 1-7 when returning to face a team that did not travel overseas the prior week. That one win was the Broncos last season, when they scored 33 4th quarter points against the Giants to win by 1 point. Fatigue will play a factor, but having home field will help significantly. This is still a Browns team that lost to the Jets on the road, and just went to the wire with the Titans. Won't be surprised if its ugly, but Pittsburgh rides the run game again into their bye. Steelers 20 Browns 17. Jason Aponte: This will be a dogfight between the division rivals. The Steelers have shown improvement offensively lately and will need to beat Cleveland's plan of man coverage. Rodgers and the offense does enough and the defense holds up to give Pittsburgh the division lead. Steelers 21, Browns 17. Ryan Parish : The Steelers were the better team in 3 out of 4 quarters the last time these teams met a few weeks ago. Both teams have found a groove since, and they enter the contest at 5-2. Winner leaves the game atop the AFC North. I've had a running bit in these predictions that will not change until it stops working. Browns 24-Steelers 23. Austin Bechtold: The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns at home in the regular season since I was two. I can't fathom it happening with how the Steelers defense is playing right now. I've been wrong about Patrick Graham and doubted his scheme to a degree early in the season, but if he calls a great gameplan Sunday I'm sold. Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since 2021. The Browns aren't the old Browns and I think are better than people are giving credit for. The Steelers do what it takes, and will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday. Steelers 24-18. Ryland Bickley : This is a series that has been defined by home teams winning as of late, and with the Steelers on a hot streak and playing in Acrisure this Sunday, I don't expect that to change. Cleveland's man coverage scheme should once again prove a challenge for the Pittsburgh offense, but the Steelers defense has taken some strides since the last matchup. Steelers 27, Browns 20 . Joey Bray : When these teams take the field on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be exactly one month removed from suffering another loss to the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Since that game, the Steelers have won three straight. I can't say for certain how much the team has grown since then, as they still have concerns in the secondary on defense and struggles in the red zone as an offense. Unlike last time where the browns jumped out to a big lead early, I think this game will be a close one throughout. The Browns are a much better football team that anyone anticipated entering the season. Todd Monken deserves a ton of credit for the way he has continued to put Deshaun Watson and the offense in positions to win. However, all five of their wins have come on game winning drives, a trend that is unlikely to continue. I'll take Pittsburgh to get their revenge on Cleveland and go into the bye week with sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Steelers 21, Browns 20 . Jarrett Bailey: I said ahead of the Saints game that I don't know if the Steelers are a team I'd bank on winning four games in a row, yet here we are after a three-game win streak. The whole "Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since 2003" doesn't necessarily mean much to me in terms of results. Although it does seem to matter when these two teams play in Cleveland that the Steelers turn into the worst versions of themselves. I do think the Steelers win, but I'm not going to take this Browns team lightly. Steelers 20, Browns 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . away.blurb: 3 Browns are questionable as team works out five players ahead of Week 8 According to ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi , the Browns worked out five players ahead of the weekend: tackle Blake Austin, guard C.J. Hanson, center Jacob Rizy, and wide receivers Xavier Weaver and Brady Boyd. Head coach Todd Monken did not rule Howard out, however. He was listed as questionable for Week 8 along with defensive back Myles Harden and safety Daniel Thomas. 2 ruled out, 1 questionable for Steelers who enter this game close to full health The Steelers are healthy as well. They ruled out a pair of depth defensive backs in Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter on Friday. Both players have mostly played on special teams for Pittsburgh. Wide receiver Ben Skowronek is questionable for Sunday with a calf injury. He’s only been targeted four times by Aaron Rodgers in five game appearances this season. Can the Browns figure out how to score in the first quarter? The Steelers enter this game allowing 4.3 points per game in the first quarter. They should be able to put the Browns’ most maddening trend to the test out of the gate. Cleveland played man-to-man on Pittsburgh’s receivers on over 70% of Rodgers’ dropbacks in Week 4. The Steelers’ inability to create quick separation, and Rodgers’ propensity to get the ball out quickly, led to a 55% completion percentage and a lot of failed drives. The Browns are becoming a bad matchup for the Steelers, and that’s why we have them grinding out another close win. Watson has been getting the ball out quicker and making sounder decisions. Cleveland has the personnel, like tight end Harold Fannin, wide receiver KC Concepcion, and running back Dylan Sampson, to turn quick passes into big gains, limiting Pittsburgh’s elite pass rush. This game could easily go the Steelers’ way if the Browns struggle with sacks and turnovers. But if they can protect the football and get it out quickly, they should be in position to win it in the fourth quarter. Week 8 is dripping with opportunity for the Cleveland Browns. This is the spot, playing in a stadium that’s been a house of horrors for decades, that turns a feel-good start to the season into something much more real. The Browns are as healthy as they’ve been all season and are playing their best football, at least in terms of stringing together all three phases. A win over Pittsburgh would clinch their first regular-season sweep in the rivalry since the 1980s and would vault their record to 6-2 atop the AFC North. Browns fans have been craving meaningful football. It doesn’t get much bigger than Sunday’s trip to Pittsburgh. From the key matchups to the injury concerns and everything in between, here’s a primer for one of the biggest games on this week’s slate. Hanson, center Jacob Rizy, and wide receivers Xavier Weaver and Brady Boyd. Head coach Todd Monken did not rule Howard out, however. He was listed as questionable for Week 8 along with defensive back Myles Harden and safety Daniel Thomas. 2 ruled out, 1 questionable for Steelers who enter this game close to full health The Steelers are healthy as well. They ruled out a pair of depth defensive backs in Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter on Friday. Both players have mostly played on special teams for Pittsburgh. Wide receiver Ben Skowronek is questionable for Sunday with a calf injury. He’s only been targeted four times by Aaron Rodgers in five game appearances this season. Can the Browns figure out how to score in the first quarter? The Steelers enter this game allowing 4.3 points per game in the first quarter. They should be able to put the Browns’ most maddening trend to the test out of the gate. Cleveland played man-to-man on Pittsburgh’s receivers on over 70% of Rodgers’ dropbacks in Week 4. The Steelers’ inability to create quick separation, and Rodgers’ propensity to get the ball out quickly, led to a 55% completion percentage and a lot of failed drives. The Browns are becoming a bad matchup for the Steelers, and that’s why we have them grinding out another close win. Watson has been getting the ball out quicker and making sounder decisions. Cleveland has the personnel, like tight end Harold Fannin, wide receiver KC Concepcion, and running back Dylan Sampson, to turn quick passes into big gains, limiting Pittsburgh’s elite pass rush. This game could easily go the Steelers’ way if the Browns struggle with sacks and turnovers. But if they can protect the football and get it out quickly, they should be in position to win it in the fourth quarter. Week 8 is dripping with opportunity for the Cleveland Browns. This is the spot, playing in a stadium that’s been a house of horrors for decades, that turns a feel-good start to the season into something much more real. The Browns are as healthy as they’ve been all season and are playing their best football, at least in terms of stringing together all three phases. A win over Pittsburgh would clinch their first regular-season sweep in the rivalry since the 1980s and would vault their record to 6-2 atop the AFC North. Browns fans have been craving meaningful football. It doesn’t get much bigger than Sunday’s trip to Pittsburgh. From the key matchups to the injury concerns and everything in between, here’s a primer for one of the biggest games on this week’s slate. home.blurb: Both teams are dealing with injuries to key players that could significantly impact Sunday's contest. Pittsburgh has several notable contributors on injured reserve who likely won't return until well after the team's bye week. However, the Steelers still have several key players whose availability bears watching as they prepare for this divisional matchup. DNP: Did not participate. LP: Limited participation. FP: Full participation. NIR: Not injury related. Friday's practice and game-status designations have not yet been provided. The Pittsburgh Steelers received encouraging news Thursday, as cornerback Ramsey, tight end Washington, outside linebacker Watt, and defensive tackle Heyward all progressed from Wednesday's non-participation to full participation. Ramsey's return to full practice is particularly important as Pittsburgh monitors its secondary ahead of its Week 8 matchup against the Cleveland Browns. However, cornerbacks Echols and Slaughter remained sidelined with hamstring injuries, leaving their availability as a key one to watch heading into Friday's practice. Highsmith and wide receiver Skowronek remained limited for a second consecutive day with groin and calf injuries, respectively. Highsmith's status warrants close attention for Pittsburgh's pass rush, while Skowronek's availability could affect the team's wide receiver depth and special teams. A win puts them within striking distance of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead, while a loss would put them even further behind this season. It should be a close one against a better Falcons team, and our panel of writers reflect that. Here are our picks for Tampa Bay's big matchup against Atlanta: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Falcons 24, Bucs 23 Despite the Bucs' dismantling of the Panthers last week, I still find it difficult to have much confidence in them heading into the matchup against the rising Atlanta Falcons. The offense can only lean on the run game for so long, so they must figure out how to attack defenses through the air. The defense and special teams have been great as of late and will need to show up in a big way again. While I do think the Bucs have a better shot at beating the Falcons now than I did a couple of weeks ago, I think the Falcons' defense will find a way to slow down the run game and force the Bucs to throw the ball. That hasn’t been great for them this year, and ultimately will be the downfall of them this week. Overall Record: 4-3 James Hill, Writer: Falcons 21, Bucs 17 Despite having a fantastic game last week, I think the Buccaneers will come back down to earth in this matchup. I don’t believe Baker Mayfield is fully healthy yet, and they drop this one because of it. Overall Record: 3-4 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 24, Falcons 21 The Buccaneers and Falcons are a fun matchup. Todd Bowles' defense has really turned it up in recent weeks, while the Falcons have several dangerous weapons on offense. Assuming Mayfield’s thumb feels quite a bit better than it did a week ago, I think the Bucs’ offense can do just enough to squeeze out a victory while extending the Bucs’ record to 2-0 in the division and narrowing the gap between them and the NFC South-leading Panthers. Logan Robinson, Founder: Bucs 28, Falcons 23 I think the Bucs do end up winning this game, and it has to do with Todd Bowles’ rush defense, which has been excellent this year. Adding that with strong secondary play and getting Antoine Winfield Jr. back to help defend Atlanta’s passing attack, it looks nice. It’s going to be a close one, but I like Tampa Bay and a bold prediction of Cade Otton having a good showing. River Wells, Editor: Falcons 24, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay didn't have to pass much against the Carolina Panthers to beat them. Atlanta has a strong rushing defense, so they won't let the Bucs beat them that way — Tampa Bay will have to go through the air. I'm still not confident that Zac Robinson's offense can do that against this Falcons team. Baker Mayfeld is still recovering from injury and BIjan Robinson can change games on his own — Bucs drop this one in Raymond James. Consensus: Falcons 3, Bucs 2 This is among the closest prediction slates we've had all year. Some of us believe the Bucs will keep the momentum going, while other writers think Tampa Bay will falter as it has multiple times this year. The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. in Tampa Bay on Nov. 1. Typically, you want to fade the previous week's results, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers just waxed the Carolina Panthers 43-13 last week. Baker Mayfield returned Sunday from a three-game absence due to a dislocated thumb and wasn't asked to do much in Tampa's victory. He completed just seven of 11 passes for 64 yards. Mayfield has the third-worst QBR this season , so I don't trust him to win by a significant margin. Meanwhile, Atlanta has better yards-per-play, early-down EPA per play, quarterback pressure rate, and explosive-play rate differentials , despite the teams having played similarly difficult schedules and both starting quarterbacks having missed time due to injuries. Falcons vs Buccaneers combo Unlike Atlanta's spread, I'm following the line movement here by taking the Under 43.5 , with the total dropping from its 45.5-point opener to the current number. Per Nfeloapp.com , Atlanta has the third-lowest pass rate over expectation, while the Bucs have the fifth-lowest rate. The forecast calls for windy, rainy conditions in Tampa on Sunday, which could hinder both passing and kicking games and make these teams more likely to lean on their rushing attacks. The matchup is still favorable. The Bucs have allowed the fifth-most touchdowns to opposing tight ends with five , while the middle of their defense has struggled in coverage. Bijan Robinson and Drake London also command plenty of attention, potentially leaving Pitts isolated against linebackers and safeties. I'll take Pitts' athleticism in those one-on-one matchups near the goal line. Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE FREDDIE FALCON MERCEDES-BENZ STADIUM Training Camp The Falcons play the Buccaneers for the first time this season on Sunday. It's their last division matchup before closing the year with three straight NFC South games. Will McFadden Senior Reporter FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The Atlanta Falcons will take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for the 66th time on Sunday, reigniting a series that has been exceptionally close. Atlanta leads the head-to-head 33-32, and each of the last six games between the two teams has been decided by six points or fewer. That includes the Falcons' 29-28 victory last season in Week 15, which featured a 15-point, fourth-quarter rally by Atlanta and a career game from tight end Kyle Pitts. Both teams head into this game off rejuvenating wins. A potent rushing attack that generated 258 yards on the ground and a defense that created four turnovers propelled the Buccaneers to a 43-13 win against the Carolina Panthers. The Falcons also forced four turnovers and got a strong performance from quarterback Michael Penix Jr. to earn a 29-20 win and hand the San Francisco 49ers their first loss of the season. After the Panthers lost to the Green Bay Packers Thursday night, the Falcons would gain sole possession of first place in the NFC South with a victory on Sunday. Here's a look at who the experts predict will win on Sunday between the Falcons and Buccaneers. away.headline: Falcons rule out 2 players, elevate 2 from practice squad vs. Bucs
away.blurb: The Atlanta Falcons made some last minute tweaks to their roster ahead of Sunday's NFC South matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . First, the team ruled out cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. and linebacker Divine Deablo. Both players sat out last weekend against the San Francisco 49ers and were listed as questionable on Atlanta's final Week 8 injury report. With Deablo out, the Falcons will turn to rookie Kendal Daniels to wear the green dot on defense. Herbert will replace Brian Robinson Jr., who was ruled out due to a hamstring injury. Check out the team's updated 53-man roster and practice squad for NFL Week 8 below. This article originally appeared on Falcons Wire: Falcons rule out 2 players, elevate 2 from practice squad vs. Bucs Daniels had a breakout performance in Week 7, recording two turnovers including the game-clinching interception in the fourth quarter. Atlanta will also look to rookie linebacker Harold Perkins Jr. to start alongside Daniels on Sunday against the Buccaneers. The Falcons also announced two practice squad elevations for some extra reinforcements. According to the team, running back Khalil Herbert and linebacker Brian Asamoah will join the team's 53-man roster in Week 8. Both players were elevated last week, and it's no surprise to see them back with the injuries at linebacker and running back. away.headline: Buccaneers vs. Falcons: Initial injury report for Week 8
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Wednesday ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, with three players sitting out practice and two others participating on a limited basis. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who continues to deal with concussion and foot injuries, was limited in practice. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also limited due to an illness. Atlanta also opened the week with several players sidelined. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not participate in practice. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith was also held out for rest. The Falcons had six players listed as limited participants, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), defensive linemen LaCale London (chest) and Charles Snowden (back), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring), cornerback Avieon Terrell (illness) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). There was some encouraging news for Tampa Bay, however. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) were both full participants Wednesday. Mayfield returned to action in last week's 43-13 victory over the Carolina Panthers, while Winfield's participation is another positive development for the Buccaneers' defense. Wide receiver Beaux Collins (hip) and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle) were full participants. Both teams will continue monitoring their injured players throughout the week, with Thursday's practice providing another indication of their progress before Friday's final injury designations. The Buccaneers (2-5) host the Falcons (3-4) on Sunday, November 1, at Raymond James Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. ET.

home.headline: Is Bucky Irving Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Buccaneers vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7)
home.blurb: Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving was limited in practice to open this week due to an illness, but he returned to a full practice session on Friday. That could lead to an expanded role for Irving, who was targeted 15 times out of the backfield in Mayfield's three starts this season. The veteran running back has been solid in the 2026 campaign, averaging 4.7 yards per carry across six games. Since then, Irving has just six total targets. So, he should have a bigger workload as a pass catcher, especially with Egbuka out. Is Bucky Irving Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Buccaneers vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7) Skip to main content ON SI As a result, the Bucs decided to take him off the injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 7 matchup with the Carolina Panthers, a sign that he'll play his usual role in this matchup. Bucky Irving (illness) not listed on injury report for Week 7. Irving's presence is great news for a 1-5 Tampa Bay team that needs every win it can get to stay alive in the NFC South and the NFC playoff picture. The Bucs are expected to get quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb) back in action on Sunday for the first time since Week 3. However, they'll be without star receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot, concussion) for the first time all season. Irving has 452 rushing yards, 74 receiving yards, two rushing scores and one receiving score this season. He'll look to build on that against a Carolina defense that has allowed the most yards per carry in the league in 2026. Let's take a look at my favorite prop for the Bucs running back now that he's set to play in Week 7. Best Bucky Irving Prop Bet vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7 Bucky Irving OVER 86.5 Rushing and Receiving Yards (-115) No team in the NFL is allowing more yards per carry this season than the Panthers (5.1), and they rank 24th in the league in EPA/Rush. So, this could be a big game for Irving, who has really come on in recent weeks, tallying 40 carries and four receptions over his last two games. Now, Irving has only cleared this line in three of his six games in 2026, but two of them came with Baker Mayfield at quarterback. Mayfield (thumb) is expected to start on Sunday, and he targeted Irving 15 times over the first three weeks of the season. The Bucs running back is averaging 4.7 yards per carry, and he could be in line for a big game against a banged-up Carolina defense. The Bucs are lacking playmakers at this point in the season, so I’ll gladly take Irving to do it all, especially since he played a season-high 85.1 percent of the team’s snaps in Week 6. home.blurb: Buccaneers vs. Falcons final injury report: Emeka Egbuka ruled out for Sunday’s game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their final injury report Friday ahead of Sunday's NFC South matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, with wide receiver Emeka Egbuka officially ruled out and two other players listed as questionable. Egbuka (foot) did not participate in Friday's practice after being limited Wednesday and Thursday. The rookie receiver has cleared concussion protocol, but his lingering foot injury will keep him sidelined for a second consecutive game. Offensive tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) returned to practice on a limited basis Friday after missing the previous two sessions. He is listed as questionable for Sunday, along with running back Kenny Gainwell (hip), who was a full participant after steadily improving throughout the week. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby and linebacker Josiah Trotter, who were both dealing with illnesses earlier in the week, also practiced fully Friday and are expected to be available. Meanwhile, Atlanta will be without running back Brian Robinson, who was ruled out with a hamstring injury after missing all three practices this week. The Falcons also have eight players listed as questionable, including defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm), defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), cornerback Avieon Terrell (illness), defensive end Charles Snowden (back) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Wide receiver Beaux Collins (hip) and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle) are also questionable despite being full participants in Friday's practice. TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka #2 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers drops a touchdown pass in the second quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. Both teams will announce their inactive players approximately 90 minutes before kickoff Sunday. The Buccaneers (2-5) host the Falcons (3-4) at Raymond James Stadium on Sunday, November 1. picks.blurb: Jaguars vs. Colts: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Jaguars vs. Colts: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 8 JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 7: Brenton Strange #85 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs the ball during the fourth quarter of an NFL 2025 game against the Indianapolis Colts at Everbank Stadium on December 7, 2025 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Gus Logue Sat, October 31, 2026 at 5:11 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Welcome to Big Cat Country's staff roundtable! This week, we're previewing the Jacksonville Jaguars' second divisional matchup of the season. They look to extend their 11-game home win streak against the rebuilding Indianapolis Colts. Question 1: What's your top question/concern about the Jaguars this week? Dillon Appleman : Can they stop playing down to their competition? In their last two games, the Jaguars have lost to the Texans and were eight seconds away from losing to the Eagles. Those two opponents have a combined record of 4-10 this season, so it's fair to question if they have a problem with elevating their game when the competition is poor. The Colts fit that same mold as a team that has basically punted on the season already, so I would like to see a more focused Jaguars team as they look to take a stranglehold over the AFC South. Travis Holmes : The Jaguars have been one of the NFL's top run-stopping defenses over the last two seasons. But as my college coach always tells me, you're only as good as your last game played. Can Anthony Campanile's unit rebound from the 114-yard rushing performance it surrendered against the Houston Texans before the bye week? One major strength-versus-strength matchup to watch is that the Jaguars rank second in the NFL in explosive rushing gains allowed, surrendering just 7 over the first six games, while the Colts' offense ranks eighth with 23. Limiting Jonathan Taylor is the first test. Eliminating the game-changing runs is the second. Gus Logue : Can Jacksonville's secondary survive without Antonio Johnson? He should be back soon from his ankle injury, but with No. 3 safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve, depth is a concern at the position. The good news is that the limping Colts probably aren't equipped to do anything about it. But could another worrisome game from the secondary spark a trade for a veteran to help solidify the unit, the way that Jakobi Meyers did for the passing offense last season? Henry Zimmer : My top questions are simply about if the Jaguars are going to add any talent at the deadline. Trades within the AFC South are not happening, but can the Jags get better by adding a player late? Defensive line help comes to mind first, but does adding someone there benefit or hurt in the long run? Question 2: What's the key to a Jaguars victory this week? Dillon : The key to a Jaguars victory is to simply keep Jonathan Taylor from wrecking the game. The Colts are just 3-6 all-time against the Jaguars with Taylor in the backfield, but all three wins have come when Taylor has gone for over 100 yards. He drives the success of that offense, so the key is to prevent a big day, which should be expected considering the Jaguars' dominance against the run under Anthony Campanille. Travis : Establishing the run game seems to be the primary focus heading into this week's matchup. The Colts rank 22nd in the league in opponent rushing yards allowed per game, and that was before Indianapolis decided to trade away interior game-wrecker DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Considering the Indianapolis front seven's struggles with missed tackles and Bhayshul Tuten's propensity to force them, this seems like a match made in heaven, especially with a potentially rainy Sunday in Duval. Gus : Quarterback play in high-leverage situations. I think we could end up looking at the box score and saying, "See, 150 rushing yards for the Jaguars and 50 rushing yards for the Colts, that's where the game was won/lost!" But really — as much as I do expect the Jaguars to have success on the ground and the Colts to struggle on the ground — Jacksonville will win because they have the better quarterback to move the chains. Henry : The key to victory this week is playing simple. This is a Colts team that is nuking itself into oblivion and should be a pushover. Don't make this game complicated and win outright. No need for jet sweeps on the half-yard line to a backup tight end. Trevor Lawrence should be out of this game in the fourth quarter. Make it simple. Question 3: Who will be an X-factor for the Jaguars this week? Dillon : I have a giant microscope over the Colts' rookie left guard, Jalen Farmer, vs. the Jaguars' interior defensive line. After the Colts traded away perennial Pro Bowler Quenton Nelson, the Colts will be starting Farmer, who has all of three offensive snaps this season. I'm looking for a big day for Arik Armstead and/or Ruke Orhorhoro on Sunday. Travis : My X-factor for this week is Jacksonville rookie left guard Emmanuel Pregnon, who will face off against Colts interior defensive linemen Grover Stewart and Adetomiwa Adebawore . Pregnon has shown major promise throughout 2026, with only a few bumps along the rookie road. Adebawore, who the Colts seem to be doubling down on moving forward following the DeForest Buckner trade, has significantly improved his hand placement and quickness in 2026. If there's an area of concern for the Jacksonville offense, it's more than likely going to come from Indianapolis' interior defensive line. Gus : Chris Rodriguez Jr., who finished with 11 carries for 55 yards in Week 6 compared to 12 carries for 39 yards for Bhayshul Tuten. I certainly expect Tuten to operate as Jacksonville's lead back moving forward, and even to have a very productive second half of the season, but don't forget about Rodriguez. Liam Coen wants this backfield to be a 1-2 punch. I could see C-Rod having a solid 50-yard, 1-TD outing on Sunday. Henry : Against a downtrodden Colts team, can the Jags manufacture some catches for Brian Thomas Jr. to potentially bolster his trade status before the deadline? This would be a lovely conspiracy if the Jags targeted BTJ upwards of a dozen times to get him maybe over 100 yards on the day and then immediately look to trade him. Strike while the iron is hot! Final score prediction? Dillon : Jaguars 30, Colts 13 Travis : Jaguars 21, Colts 13 Gus : Jaguars 26, Colts 9 Henry : Jaguars 35, Colts 10 What are your Week 8 predictions, Jaguars fans? away.headline: Week 8 Final Injury Report: Colts Welcome Back Key Starters
away.blurb: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Justin Walley (27) smiles Saturday, Aug. 1, 2026, during day four of Indianapolis Colts training camp at Grand Park in Westfield. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect OUT: Most notable for the Colts, both Sauce Gardner and Tyler Warren are off the injury report and will play in Jacksonville. Both had missed last Sunday’s loss to the Vikings; Warren missed the prior loss to Tennessee as well. Both provide much-needed boosts to a passing attack and secondary that are currently fairly thin, especially with Anthony Gould and Justin Walley both set to sit out. Gould, Indy’s primary punt returner, likely gives away to special teams ace Ashton Dulin in the return game. Walley’s absence is significant given the Colts’ backup nickel Cam Taylor-Britt is on injured reserve. It will likely be up to rookie Kapena Gushiken to hold down the slot, though defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo may switch up personnel to account for the lack of options there. Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (3) is introduced before an NFL football matchup at EverBank Stadium on Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026, in Jacksonville, Fla. The Jaguars defeated the Patriots 35-6. [Corey Perrine/Florida Times‑Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect OUT: Jacksonville takes the slight edge in terms of health going into Sunday's matchup as just Antonio Johnson has been ruled out. The Jaguars list Jalen Huskey, a rookie who’s yet to appear in a game this season, as the backup strong safety, though third-string Kaevon Merriweather has much more NFL experience and is more likely to receive the start. Still, when Merriweather eventually rotates out, Indy’s pass game must test Huskey in his first professional action. Jakobi Meyers is listed as questionable with hamstring and ankle issues. He logged back-to-back limited practices Wednesday and Thursday but missed practice Friday, making his status for the weekend unclear. If Meyers is eventually ruled out, the pressure will be on Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. to pick up the slack. Thomas had a stellar rookie season but has been on the decline ever since. He’s started only three of Jacksonville’s six games so far, recording just nine catches. away.headline: Colts' injury report includes good news on Tyler Warren, Sauce Gardner, bad news on Justin Walley
away.blurb: Starting outside cornerback Sauce Gardner is set to return after missing time with a calf injury. Starting tight end Tyler Warren will also return to play after being sidelined for two games with a groin injury. Indianapolis will be without starting slot corner Justin Walley , who suffered a knee injury late in Sunday’s road loss to the Vikings and did not practice this week, as well as the team’s first corner off the bench, veteran Cam Taylor-Britt , who landed on injured reserve this week with a groin injury also suffered late in Sunday’s 16-10 loss. The Colts will also get back starting tight end Tyler Warren , who missed the team’s last two games with a groin injury. Warren logged his first practice of any kind Thursday after suffering the injury Oct. 23 before a Week 6 game against the Titans where he didn’t appear as a game-time decision. Warren, the team’s leader in catches (30), missed all of last week’s practice, too, as well as the Week 7 game. He was limited in Thursday’s practice but then participated fully Friday. Along with Walley, the Colts also ruled out wide receiver Anthony Gould for Sunday’s game as the return specialist continues to work his way back from a concussion suffered in Week 6. Gould returned to practice this week and was full both days but needs to clear the league’s concussion protocol. Tight end Drew Ogletree (knee) and Bryce Boettcher (groin) are listed as questionable for Sunday’s game. Ogletree was limited in Thursday’s practice and then did not participate Friday, and Boettcher missed both outings after practicing once last week but missing Sunday’s Week 7 game. With Boettcher’s role Sunday in question, all signs point to rookie linebacker C.J. Allen making his first start of his NFL career, as he returns from an ankle injury he suffered last week in practice that sidelined him Sunday. Allen was a full participant in both the Colts’ practices this week. home.blurb: Jaguars-Colts Final Injury Report: Antonio Johnson Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Jaguars-Colts Final Injury Report: Antonio Johnson Ruled Out The Jacksonville Jaguars secondary could be stretched Sunday, as the team has ruled out safety Antonio Johnson for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. Johnson (ankle) did not practice on Friday after initially suffering his ankle injury in the second quarter of the team's Week 6 London matchup versus the Houston Texans. His absence clearly puts more pressure on a safety room that has already dealt with attrition earlier this season with Eric Murray, who dealt with a Week 4 concussion that kept him out of Week 5. Those combined injuries, between weeks 5 and 6 resulted in safety Kaevon Merriweather playing increased snaps on defense: With Johnson now out, the expectation is that Merriweather will receive his first start of the 2026 season. Liam Coen discussed Merriweather in Friday's media availability. In addition to the Johnson update, wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) also did not practice on Friday and is listed as questionable, though he spoke with Florida Times Union's Demetrius Harvey following practice, advising that he "felt okay." Meyers was listed on Wednesday and Thursday's injury report as a limited participant with only a hamstring issue, before sitting out Friday's session with an additional ankle issue that would have presumably occurred on Thursday. His status could come down to game day, with rain and a wet field in the forecast for Sunday. Running back LeQuint Allen Jr. (hamstring), defensive end Josh Hines-Allen (ankle), linebacker Jahlani Tavai (hamstring), and long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) were all limited on Friday and carry no game-day injury designation. Additionally, cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring), defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro (ankle), and tight end Brenton Strange (eye) were each full participants and expected to play. Notably, there has been no update on the 21-Day windows being opened for offensive lineman Patrick Mekari (back), rotational edge BJ Green (elbow), or rookie defensive end Zach Durfee (upper body). Each player has been on the injured reserve for at least four weeks, with the potential to return as the team comes off the Week 7 bye week. The Colts, on Friday, ruled out wide receiver and starting punt returner Anthony Gould (concussion). Gould is out even though he practiced fully on Thursday and Friday. Additionally, starting slot cornerback Justin Walley (knee) is out Sunday after not practicing all week. Starting linebacker Bryce Boettcher (groin) and tight end Drew Ogletree (knee) are both questionable. Boettcher has not practiced all week. Johnson has not practiced for the Jaguars this week, being listed as a non-particpant in all three practices. Jaguars-Colts Friday Injury Report: 1 Player Must Step Up in Antonio Johnson's Absence Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars will be without a big piece of their defense against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. The Jaguars have seen their safety group get hit with injuries at different points this season, and Merriweather has been one veteran who has helped steady the waters. The fourth-year safety signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2023 and appeared in 42 games with the Buccaneers in three seasons. This included 14 games with the Buccaneers in 2024 when Jaguars head coach Liam Coen was the team's offensive coordinator. “Need Kaevon to continue to step up and evolve. But being with him in Tampa, he was a guy that really helped on teams and played his tail off there but was also able to step in and he started, I think, like eight games for us that year in ‘24 at safety. The game wasn't too big for him," Coen said on Friday. Merriweather also spent time with the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions during parts of his career, and he signed to the Jaguars practice squad early in September. He was eventually moved up to the active roster, and he now looks like he will have to play a significant role in some facet against the Colts at home on Sunday. "And then when you went and watched him transition to Houston and then watched him throughout the preseason and the regular season on special teams, you could tell he took on some of the identity and ways in which Houston plays," Coen said. "That physicality, running to the football, burning it down and going and playing your ass off. That was something that was intriguing for us as well. And I've always just thought the game wasn't ever too big for Kaevon, never really got too high, too low. picks.headline: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. picks.blurb: Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup Cameron DaSilva, Rams Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 1:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams are taking on the Los Angeles Chargers this Sunday in their first meeting since the 2022 season. The Rams are 3-4 and looking to get back to .500, while the Chargers are still searching for their first win. To preview this game, we caught up with Chargers Wire's Gavino Borquez and asked him five questions about the team, including a final score prediction. What on earth has happened to Justin Herbert and this offense? What's gone so wrong with Mike McDaniel as the OC? Chargers Wire: The Chargers sit at 0-6 and rank dead last in the NFL in points per game (15.0) and EPA per play (-0.190). Herbert is playing the worst football of his seven seasons in the league. He has thrown 5 touchdowns and thrown 8 interceptions, tying for the league high, and has taken 21 sacks. The issues are layered. The offensive line and wide receiver group have been ravaged by injuries. Pre-snap penalties have hindered the unit. And the marriage between Herbert and McDaniel's scheme has not clicked. The two spent roughly four hours in film sessions during the bye week working on mutual accountability and finding spots to build on. We will see if it comes together on Sunday. Are there any key players the Chargers are getting back from injury this week coming off the bye? Chargers Wire: Right tackle Joe Alt is officially cleared and returning to the lineup after missing time with a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has been a full participant in practice coming out of the bye, though still navigating final clearance from a concussion, and is expected to play. Who's an underrated player on defense that the Rams should know about? Chargers Wire: While the average casual fan might not know his name, defensive tackle Teair Tart is widely respected by offensive linemen as a player they need to account for. Tart is known for his run defense prowess, but he has flashed effectively in generating interior pressure. Do the Chargers have any playmakers who can threaten the Rams defense besides Ladd McConkey? Chargers Wire: The Chargers don't possess an alpha weapon, but second-year Tre' Harris has flashed potential as a reliable deep threat . In 5 games, he has caught 15 passes on 26 targets for 225 yards, averaging an efficient 15.0 yards per reception. Though his momentum was temporarily paused by an injury suffered in Week 5 that forced him to miss the Week 6 game against the Chiefs, Harris is trending towards on Sunday. Who wins on Sunday and what's the final score? Chargers Wire: While the Chargers benefit from the return of key offensive pieces in Joe Alt and Ladd McConkey, their vulnerability lies right up the middle. The Bolts' struggling interior offensive line is poised to be the Achilles' heel in this game, allowing the Rams' defensive front to consistently collapse the pocket and get to Justin Herbert. Furthermore, even with the Chargers coming off a bye week, it's hard to tell whether they've made any meaningful offensive changes. Expect the Rams to exploit the center of the line and for their balanced offense to score three touchdowns to secure the victory. Rams 24, Chargers 16. away.headline: Two Key Chargers Players Will Return to Action in Week 8 Versus the Rams
away.blurb: Safety Derwin James Jr. remains out with a hamstring injury. This week, he reportedly had a setback, and as a result, head coach Jim Harbaugh said he’s a candidate to go on injured reserve. Left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) also won’t play. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley, both of whom have hamstring injuries, are questionable for Sunday’s contest. Garrett will be out on Sunday, as will wide receiver Davante Adams. At times, the Rams have struggled defensively — they gave up 302 passing yards last week against the Las Vegas Raiders — so perhaps there is a slight opening for the Bolts to find some success. There isn’t a whole lot the Los Angeles Chargers can do right now, or even by the end of the season, to play a lot better. The most immediate thing that would help is for them to become healthier. Starting right tackle Joe Alt hasn’t played since Week 4 against the Seattle Seahawks due to a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey suffered a concussion during L.A.’s last game, which was a 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6, and he entered concussion protocol as a result. Both men returned to practice for the Chargers this week, and there is good news about their status for this Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. Alt and McConkey are on the mend In the Chargers’ final injury report for Sunday’s game, neither Alt nor McConkey are listed, which means both are expected to play, per Noah Furtado of The Athletic. While the Chargers are 0-6 and have been a disaster, the Rams haven’t exactly lived up to expectations either. The Rams have a 3-4 record despite being strong favorites to win the Super Bowl championship when the season started, and while they have had some injuries, such as the one that reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett is dealing with, they have their own problems. The Bolts currently rank last in the NFL in points per game, 28th in passing yards and last in turnovers. Quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions heading into Week 8 with eight, against just five touchdown passes. away.headline: Chargers’ nightmare season gets even worse with brutal Derwin James injury update
away.blurb: Los Angeles heads back to SoFi Stadium but this time will come out of the visitors locker room. That's because they're the away team when they take on the Rams on Sunday. Chargers’ nightmare season gets even worse with brutal Derwin James injury update - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Lorenzo J. Reyna, ClutchPoints Wed, October 28, 2026 at 9:18 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Los Angeles Chargers feature roster concerns amid their 0-6 start to the 2026 NFL season . Now coach Jim Harbaugh and his staff must find a new safety. All thanks to a brutal Derwin James update on the NFL injury front. The All-Pro defender has hit a roadblock with his recovery, per Harbaugh. He might have to go on injured reserve as his hamstring isn't fully healed. James has suited up in just three games for the winless Bolts, hitting 12 solo tackles. James has totaled 21 tackles across the three contests he's been healthy for but has broken up one pass only. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) But nothing has looked healthy for the Chargers. James is among the litany of injuries on the Bolts. Star wide receiver Ladd McConkey didn't practice on Monday as he recovers from a concussion. Fellow wideout Brennen Thompson also is dealing with an injury, with his quadriceps as the issue. However, Tre Harris looks ready to come back from his hamstring injury. Which can become a huge boost for struggling quarterback Justin Herbert, who has thrown more interceptions at eight compared to touchdown passes with five. But the Chargers, again, face potential roster tinkering ahead of the league's trade deadline. Herbert has risen as a possible trending trade contender, especially with the Seattle Seahawks becoming linked as a possibility there . away.headline: Chargers Star Suffers Injury Setback Amid Challenging Season
away.blurb: If that move is made this week, that means James would be out of commission until at least Nov. 29. Chargers Star Suffers Injury Setback Amid Challenging Season - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Chargers Star Suffers Injury Setback Amid Challenging Season Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads This season has gone from bad to worse for the Los Angeles Chargers, and one of the Bolts' defensive stars may not be around to help right the ship. Safety Derwin James Jr., who's missed the Chargers' last three games with a nagging hamstring injury, now may be headed to injured reserve, head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday. What's wrong with Derwin James? As detailed by Elliott Teaford of the Orange County Register , the move to place James on IR isn't official yet, but Harbaugh said "it's looking like he may go to IR." Jun 17, 2026; El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James (3) during minicamp at The Bolt. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) He'd miss games against the LA Rams, Houston Texans, Baltimore Ravens and New York Jets, but could come back to play against the New England Patriots. It's a devastating blow for a team in desperate need of a spark, particularly given the expectations placed upon James this offseason. The Chargers rewarded James' elite play with a huge contract extension that made him the highest paid safety in the NFL for the second time in his career. Between James' injury and a struggling offense, though, the Chargers are now the last winless team in the NFL. What does Derwin James mean to the Chargers? So far this season, James' stats haven't exactly jumped off the page. In his three games, he had 21 tackles and broke up a pass. Those numbers, though, belie a spectacular resume thus far. Nov 30, 2025; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James Jr. (3) reacts against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Over his career, which includes parts or all of eight seasons, he has 12 interceptions, 47 passes broken up, six forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries and 19 sacks, according to Football Reference . In the six seasons in which he's played at least 14 games, he's been a Pro Bowler five times and an All Pro four times. That kind of production and experience is impossible to replace, and this Sunday, Matthew Stafford and the Rams might have a field day with the Bolts defense. Considering the Rams are also looking to rebound from a poor start to the year, this battle for LA supremacy might be the defining week for both franchises. Do you think the Chargers can get their first win of the season without Derwin James? The post Chargers Star Suffers Injury Setback Amid Challenging Season appeared first on LA Sports Report .

home.headline: Chargers Injury Report: No changes from Bolts’ 2nd day of Rams prep
home.blurb: Offensive guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) and wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) were once again non-participants. There was hope both could return this week, but they're slated to miss yet another week at this rate. Receivers Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) were full and limited, respectively. Having Harris back out there will be huge for the offense, but recent history tells us we can't be confident in McConkey's return lasting all that long. Cornerback Rodney Shelley is on pace to return from a hamstring injury and the Chargers will need him with fellow corner Deane Leonard still rehabbing a concussion. Veteran Donte Jackson returning to the field would also be huge for the cornerback room that continues to be wiped out by injuries. home.headline: Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8
home.blurb: Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8 The Los Angeles Rams could be managing several injuries in Week 8 as they take on the Los Angeles Charger s. Center Coleman Shelton, tight end Colby Parkinson, wide receiver Jordan Whittington, and cornerback Trent McDuffie were all listed as questionable for Sunday's game while long snapper Joe Cardona was listed as doubtful. Shelton is one of the bigger names on that list given his role as the starting center on the offensive line. Shelton was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday. Another player the Rams will be closely watching heading into Sunday's game is McDuffie, who has missed the last two weeks with a groin injury. While McDuffie was a limited participant in practice all week, he will be listed as questionable against the Chargers. McVay was hopeful about McDuffie going into Sunday, but the Rams can feel confident with the players behind him as Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have each played well. Additionally, Parkinson didn't participate in practice all week. If Parkinson is out, it would likely leave the Rams with just Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and Max Klare at tight end and limit what the offense could do out of 13 personnel. Parkinson is extremely valuable in those formations, especially with his ability as a blocker in the run game. Popping up on the injury report on Friday was Whittington. McVay noted that Whittington's back locked up in practice, which is why he'll be listed as questionable. On the Chargers' side, they'll be without guard Kayode Awosika, safety Derwin James Jr., defensive back Deane Leonard, and wide receiver Brenan Thompson. All four players have been ruled out. Additionally, cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley will be questionable with hamstring injuries. home.headline: Rams-Chargers injury report: Latest on Trent McDuffie, Nate Landman
home.blurb: While Garrett and Ferguson won't return this week , Trent McDuffie and Nate Landman are both trending up. McDuffie will be a limited participant on Wednesday, while Landman has cleared the concussion protocol and will be a full participant. Coleman Shelton will miss practice due to a hip injury, and Colby Parkinson is also being held out because of a rib injury. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training. Meanwhile, after starting the season 5-0, the Chiefs just suffered their first loss of the season to the Seattle Seahawks last week — a team the Broncos defeated the week prior. Now, the Chiefs head to Mile High to try to get back on the horse and avoid a two-game losing streak. The 5-2 Broncos have won three in a row, and after sweeping the Chiefs last year, they're looking to balance the scales this season . A win would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West and put them on a path to repeating as division champs, especially given Kansas City's remaining schedule. How will this Broncos-Chiefs rematch shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding at Mile High. Denver has weathered a very tough schedule to open the 2026 season, beating the Los Angeles Rams, Seattle Seahawks, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers and Arizona Cardinals to begin the year at 5-2. While Denver’s offense has not been great (22nd in EPA/Play), the defense is a top-10 unit once again. Nix and Co. seemed to find a rhythm in a win over Arizona in Week 7, and they’ll look to carry that into a home date against Mahomes and the one-loss Chiefs. Kansas City dominated Denver at home in Week 1, winning by three touchdowns, but it’s coming off a shaky performance against the Seattle Seahawks in a loss in Week 7. The Chiefs are still 5-1 this season, but they scored just three points in their last game and failed to reach the red zone on a single possession. Will a Denver defense that has been red hot in recent weeks be able to slow down Kenneth Walker III and this Chiefs attack? All season long, the SI Betting team has been sharing final score predictions as a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, we’ve hit a few exact scores, which can make for a fun long shot bet from time to time during the season. With a ton at stake in this matchup – including first place in the AFC West – here’s a look at my prediction for the Chiefs vs. Broncos rematch in Week 8. Chiefs vs. Broncos Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chiefs -1.5 (-105) Broncos +1.5 (-115) Broncos: -102 40.5 (Over -112/Under -108) There hasn’t been much movement in the odds for this game, as the Chiefs opened as 1.5-point road favorites even with their loss to Seattle on Sunday night. The total has dropped a point from 41.5 to 40.5, and it’s worth noting that the UNDER hit in this matchup in Week 1 with the Chiefs winning 31-10. Chiefs vs. Broncos Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for every single game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s buying the Chiefs on the road in this AFC West showdown: The Broncos' offensive issues and Bo Nix's play are going to haunt them against a good defense sooner rather than later. Their offense is 23rd in EPA per play and 29th in success rate, making them one of the worst offenses in the league through the first seven weeks. Now they take on a Chiefs team that has been impressive defensively, ranking fifth in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. I'd like to see the Chiefs' offense lean on the run game even more moving forward, as they rank in the top three in every offensive rushing metric. They can use that weapon against a Broncos defense that has struggled to stop the run compared to recent seasons. They're 27th in opponent rush EPA. If the Chiefs can lean on their run game and continue to play good defense, they're going to get the road win and cover the short spread. A lot of this game comes down to two things: Do you believe in the Denver offense after a strong Week 7? And, how much stock do you put into Kansas City’s Week 1 win at home? The Broncos are still just 22nd in EPA/Play, 29th in success rate and 26th in yards per play on offense. That isn’t going to cut it against Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker III, especially since Denver is allowing 4.6 yards per carry on defense. These teams are No. 5 (Kansas City) and No. 6 (Denver) in EPA/Play on the defensive side of the ball, and the UNDER has hit in the majority of both of their games. I expect another low-scoring affair with the Chiefs’ offense ultimately being the better unit on Sunday. away.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
away.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. He missed the team's previous two games with a hamstring injury. Rice is expected to play against the Denver Broncos on Sunday after returning to practice this week. His availability gives Patrick Mahomes another receiving option. The Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice returned to full participation in practice this week following a hamstring injury. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported that Rice has no injury designation for the Week 8 matchup. Head coach Andy Reid also confirmed on October 30 that Rice would play. Sep 14, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice (4) kicks the ball after scoring a touchdown against the Denver Broncos during the game at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Schefter wrote, "Chiefs WR Rashee Rice has no injury designation status for Sunday and is expected to play Sunday vs. the Broncos." The Chiefs selected Rice in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft with the 55th overall pick. He played college football at Southern Methodist University before joining to the Chiefs. Rice recorded 79 receptions for 938 yards and seven touchdowns in 16 games during his rookie season in 2023. His reception and touchdown totals set Chiefs rookie records. He also had more than 100 receiving yards in two games. In the playoffs, Rice caught eight passes for 130 yards and two touchdowns against the Miami Dolphins in the Wild Card round. He finished the postseason with 26 receptions for 262 yards, setting franchise rookie records in both categories. Rice appeared in four games in 2024, recording 24 receptions for 288 yards and two touchdowns. In 2025, he played eight games and finished with 53 receptions for 571 yards and five touchdowns, along with 20 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown. Rice injured his hamstring during the Chiefs' Week 4 game against the Las Vegas Raiders. He missed the rest of that game and the team's next two matchups. After a Week 5 bye, Kansas City faced the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6 and the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7. The Chiefs went 1-1 in the two games Rice missed, defeating the Chargers 22-6 before losing 20-3 to the Seahawks. During that stretch, Xavier Worthy recorded 10 receptions for 84 yards. Can they make it three wins on the year this week down in South Florida? Historically, playing against the Miami Dolphins on the road has been a tall task for the Patriots. The heat, plus struggles against a team that's either been very good or very bad, hasn't led to the best of results for New England. This year, however, should be a solid victory for the Patriots — despite the conditions. "We have to be conditioned," head coach Mike Vrabel said this week. "I think the better that we play, the more we possess the ball, the fresher we'll stay defensively. Hopefully we get the receivers into a rotation. The backs, we rotate. I don't think that the offensive linemen will necessarily rotate. We may play a couple guys based on who's available. That remains to be seen. The edge guys, we rotate. We try to rotate along the defensive line. We like to have our best players available to help us win." Ahead of Week 8, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right? Hurwitz: What Patriots Offense Will We Get?
