Brown questionable with a knee and ankle injury, plus TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an illness , we don't know just yet about how the offense will look. Can the running game bounce back and start to put together a big game? Will the passing attack look good, regardless of who's out there? That's how this game will be dictated. X-Factor: QB Drake Maye Last week against the Chicago Bears, Maye had an excellent day — passing for two touchdowns and running in a third. That was against a Bears defense that's in Super Bowl conversations. Against a Miami defense that has struggled all year, the 24-year-old should have a comfortable day in the pocket, even if some starters at both offensive line and wide receiver aren't playing. Final Score Prediction: Patriots 26, Dolphins 10 I don't see the Patriots eclipsing 30+ points considering how depleted their wide receiving corps is right now. But they certainly should win this game by several scores. The Dolphins will keep it close for a bit , but the extended break for the Patriots should help them get back in the winning swing of things. Ventola: They’re TANKING!! However, I frankly do not see a world where that happens again on Sunday. The Dolphins are not a good football team. In fact, there is an argument to be made that they are the worst in the league. Last week, Miami scraped out with its first game of the season against a lowly New York Jets squad. However, I frankly do not see a world where that happens again on Sunday. Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis has just 1,057 yards and four touchdowns through the air this season, sitting 25th and 27th in the NFL, respectively. Plus, Miami’s fifth-leading receiver, Ryan Miller, is now on New England’s practice squad. All of that to say, the Dolphins are much better off losing this game — to continue plummeting toward an early draft pick — than they are winning it. X-Factor: WR Efton Chism III Final Score Prediction: Patriots 23, Dolphins 10 Sunday afternoon may be a snooze fest. Between the Patriots’ depleted offense and the Dolphins untalented offense, I do not expect many points to be put on the board. Whichever team can play cleaner, more complementary football should come out with the win. All in all, I trust Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel to instill that significantly more than I trust first-year Dolphins lead man Jeff Hafley. With that in mind, I asked the following question this past week: What are your predictions, bold or otherwise, for the Miami Dolphins' defense and offense in this coming Sunday's game vs. the New England Patriots? Who do you expect to lead the team in key categories like tackles, tackles for loss, pass breakups, interceptions, defensive touchdowns, etc., on defense, and receiving yards, touchdowns, receptions, rushing production, and first downs, etc., on offense? What are your stat-line projections for our key playmakers this week, and/or who will be the team's MVPs on each side of the ball? Below are some of your takes and predictions for tomorrow's game- DalFinsFan is rightfully curious about this oddity in the schedule that seemingly helps a team from a colder climate that just happens to be the Pats. Curious why this is a late game instead of a 1:00pm ko. dedstrk says make it mistake-free and maybe? We need mistake free football and for the Pats to not take the Dolphins seriously enough for most of the game. Run the ball and continue on with the explosives and running the ball for first downs with Malik and OG. Phinette says the route to victory is keeping the ball out of the Pats' offense's hands. Our best shot at pulling off the upset is by controlling the clock. We need to stick with our ground game and avoid the costly three and outs. On defense we have to avoid being torched by the deep ball. If we can force the Pats to grind it out we have a shot. Phoenix6 has Miami narrowly edging out NE for victory #2. Defense: 1 sack, 1 fumble recovery, 2 interceptions. Rodriguez MVP. Offense: Ollie 89yds, 1 TD. Malik 289yds passing, 49yds rushing, 3 TDs. Douglas MVP. Dolphins 🐬 28, Patriots 27. coluccim believes that bad weather would be our best friend on Sunday. Our pass D is god awful, really. Pray for rain Phins1972 is much more focused on the rookies' development across the roster over the final score. We got our one win, and at this point I'm less concerned with the scoreboard than I am with seeing which players take a step forward and which ones don't. I really wish there were a young edge rusher on the roster who looked like a legitimate developmental piece. I'm still not a believer in Chop Robinson. He's played better lately, and credit where it's due, but I'm not sold yet. I'm interested to see whether Caleb Douglas can build on his recent performance and make an impact again. It would also be encouraging to see Chris Bell put together a solid outing. On the ground, I'd love to see Ollie top 100 yards once more. If Miami gets one of those hot, humid afternoons, a big back consistently moving the chains could have Patriots defenders gasping for air by the fourth quarter. If they can keep the game reasonably competitive, that'll be a positive. At this stage, player development is every bit as important as the final score, if not more so. Pats will attempt to shutdown Miamis run game forcing the Dolphins into passing situations. The Pats have a much better secondary than the Phins. Best bet for Miami is to hope Maye is sloppy and throws a couple picks and loses a fumble or two. The Pats are coming off a 10 day break and are not taking a Miami victory for granted. Should be a fairly close entertaining game. The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The assignment this week doesn't compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets. Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel 's team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road. As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That's what should happen in this game. Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors. Even in the prime years of Tom Brady's leadership, the Patriots have regularly been pushed hard by the Dolphins. The Patriots are 17-40 all-time in games played in Miami. Maye will not take the Dolphins lightly. He should be close to his best because he appears to have overcome the poor start he had in early season games in Seattle and Jacksonville. Maye has risen quite a bit in the ranks of NFL quarterbacks after his early struggles. He has completed 141 of 214 passes for 1,784 yards with 13 TDs and 8 interceptions. Maye's ability to get away from the pass rush is a big part of his game. He has run for 211 yards and 2 TDs, but the most important part of his athleticism is his ability to get away from the pass rush and get the ball to his receivers. It seems very unlikely that the Dolphins secondary is going to stop tight end Hunter Henry along with wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. The big question revolves around A.J. Brown. He has been limited by injuries this season and has played just three game and has caught just 9 passes for 101 yards. He may or may not be ready to contribute to the Patriots' effort in this game because his knee appears to have flared up. However, the Patriots are expecting him to become their go-to receiver at one point this season. Malik Willis will throw for 150 yards, but toss two interceptions Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Vrabel wants to see his defense step up quite a bit in the weeks to come. When the Patriots made their charge last season, Maye and the offense got a big assist from the defense as it stepped up by forcing takeaways. The Pats are going to attempt to do this by putting pressure on QB Malik Willis. The former Packer has tried to keep the Dolphins afloat, but the Dolphins have just one win this season. Willis has completed 87 of 151 passes for 1,057 yards with a 4-4 TD-interception ratio. He has also rushed for 223 yards and 3 TDs. Willis has been sacked 16 times this season, and linebacker Elijah Ponder of the Patriots will be after him. Ponder leads New England with 5.5 sacks and should get at least 1.5 in this game. Willis will be trying to get the ball to Malik Washington. He leads the Dolphins with 26 receptions for 289 yards but he has yet to find the end zone. Bold game prediction: Patriots 33, Dolphins 13 The Patriots have too much talent and they are focused on playing consistent, error-free football from this point forward. While many Patriots teams have had problems on the road against the Dolphins, this team will not. Look for Maye and RB Rhamondre Stevenson to get the Patriots off to a good start, and the defense will keep the Dolphins from mounting a charge. The Patriots will have control of this game prior to the end of the third quarter and New England will gain its fourth win in five games. away.headline: Patriots lose AJ Brown to injury again, rule out other offensive players ahead of matchup with division rival
away.blurb: New England’s offense will be shorthanded Sunday, with three players ruled out for the Patriots divisional game against the Miami Dolphins. The Patriots ruled out wide receiver A.J. Brown because of ankle and knee injuries, running back TreVeyon Henderson because of an illness and offensive tackle Marcus Bryant because of an ankle injury. All three players had been listed as questionable before being ruled out. For Brown, the setback comes after he i njured his ankle in the season opener and spent the next four games on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain. He returned to play in each of the past two games. Brown went down after a Seahawks defender rolled into him and remained on the field after the play. After medical personnel tended to Brown on the field, he made his way to the sideline without assistance. He was later ruled out for the remainder of the game because of what was described as an ankle injury. He finished that night with three catches for 26 yards. The Week 8 matchup with the Dolphins will be Henderson’s second missed game this season. He sat out the season opener with an ankle injury Bryant has been on injured reserve through the season, but was designated to return and was a full participant in practice all week. Original article source: Patriots lose AJ Brown to injury again, rule out other offensive players ahead of matchup with division rival Brown appeared to suffer the injury while attempting to make a catch at Lumen Field against the Seattle Seahawks on Sept. 9 during the NFL’s first regular-season game played on a Wednesday. The matchup was billed as a rematch of Super Bowl LX , which Seattle won in February by defeating New England 29-10 to claim the franchise’s second Vince Lombardi Trophy. After an uneven 2025 season for both Brown and the Eagles' offense, Philadelphia traded him to the Patriots for a pair of future draft picks amid signs that his once-close friendship and productive on-field partnership with quarterback Jalen Hurts had deteriorated. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

away.headline: Patriots hit with double dose of bad injury news day before Dolphins game
away.blurb: The Patriots listed running back TreVeyon Henderson as questionable to play the Dolphins due to an illness on the final injury report on Friday. New England also listed wide receiver A.J. Brown as questionable to play due to knee and ankle injuries. Both players did not participate in practice on Thursday or Friday. Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Patriots downgraded Brown and Henderson to out on Saturday. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks that kept him out until New England played the New York Jets in Week 6. On Friday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the knee injury Brown is dealing with this week is separate from the high-ankle sprain injury he suffered against Seattle. He wasn’t able to finish practice on Wednesday. “Just like everything else, when you come out of the game or a long week or practice on Monday, you evaluate the player,” Vrabel said , via the Patriots’ website. “He just wasn’t able to practice or finish practice on Wednesday. So, we’ll continue to treat him, and then we’ll see where he is tomorrow.” The New England Patriots will be down two key offensive players when they travel to play the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. The Patriots are 4-3 coming off a 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears on “Thursday Night Football” in Week 7. Henderson had just nine yards on three carries against Chicago. It's been a largely disappointing first half of the season for wide receiver A.J. Brown in his debut campaign with the New England Patriots . Things are possibly about to get worse for the Patriots and their marquee offseason trade acquisition. New England could potentially afford to sit Brown in Week 8 if he's not healthy enough, as the Patriots are heavy road favorites for Sunday's contest versus the Miami Dolphins. New England has a pair of NFC North contenders on deck in Weeks 9 and 10 with the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, respectively, before its Week 11 bye. The Patriots are just 4-3 this fall, however, so if they want to make a run at their second straight AFC East crown and put pressure on the Buffalo Bills (5-1), they can't take the Dolphins for granted. Brown has played in just three of New England's first seven contests this year as he missed Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 5 due to a high-ankle sprain. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to action in Week 6 against the New York Jets but has yet to have an impact on offense. Brown has played only 132 offensive snaps in his three games and has recorded nine catches for 101 scoreless yards on 20 targets. His longest reception of the season has gone for just 18 yards, but Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday that he isn't concerned about the 29-year-old's lack of production. Thursday's news still leaves the door open for Brown to take the field and perhaps turn things around on Sunday, but it's not looking great.

home.headline: Patriots vs. Dolphins Wednesday injury report: Ben Brown returns, while Carlton Davis III ramps up
home.blurb: The starting right guard returned for Wednesday’s practice after missing one week and one game because of a knee injury. Also more than present was starting cornerback Carlton Davis III, who had been limited before being ruled out for a third consecutive matchup due to a neck injury stemming from September. Every member of the Patriots’ active roster was on hand for Wednesday’s practice coming out of the mini bye. For the 2025 AFC East winners, that hadn’t been the case on any injury report since the start of the regular season. Among four practicing in a limited capacity — along with a Pro Bowl wide receiver sharing the same last name — Ben Brown had been ruled out during what became a 26-19 win over the New York Jets and was listed as a non-participant leading up to what became a 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears. And with a hamstring injury sending fellow interior starter Alijah Vera-Tucker to injured reserve prior to the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, August trade acquisition Walter Rouse and October signing Matt Pryor stayed in next to center Jared Wilson at Soldier Field. OT Marcus Bryant (ankle — IR return “Not trying to rush the process, but really trying to be efficient at recovering and being able to get back out there and be a guy that my team can depend on,” Davis told reporters of his three-game absence on Wednesday. “I think the worst is just sitting on the sideline watching plays being made or being a bystander. Last year I played in every game, so this year I was looking to do the same. home.blurb: Vera-Tucker exited in the second quarter of New England's Week 6 victory over his former team, the New York Jets , on Oct. 18 and did not return. New England ruled him out for Thursday night's game against the Chicago Bears, according to ESPN , then moved him to injured reserve Oct. 22 . That designation sidelines him for Weeks 7 through 10 at minimum, with a return at least possible in Week 12 after the bye. Before the move, he had started five games and 340 offensive snaps , according to The Boston Globe . Injuries, unfortunately, have shaped his career. A torn right triceps ended his 2022 season in Week 7, according to Sportsforecaster.com , and a torn Achilles did the same in Week 5 of 2023. He started 15 games in 2024 , then tore his left triceps in practice before Week 1 of 2025, wiping out his entire season . The injury epidemic cost the unit continuity and depth. That has thrust some lesser-known players into big roles, especially with Jalen Hurts out for the season with a blood clot. Backup quarterback Tanner McKee is set to make his third consecutive start, and the Eagles are looking to snap a five-game losing streak that has dropped them into third place in the division. Meanwhile, the Commanders are coming out of their bye week and looking to get back on track after a loss on Monday Night Football in Week 6 to the San Francisco 49ers. Jayden Daniels and company lost Terry McLaurin to a knee injury for the rest of the season in that matchup, which should lead to some new faces carrying the load for Washington at receiver. That opens the door for some interesting decisions in the anytime touchdown scorer market, and I've decided on three players that I like to score with these two rivals facing off. Overall, Barkley has suited up for just 32.8 percent of the Eagles’ offensive plays in the five games he’s appeared in, making him a risky bet elsewhere in the prop market. The star back played less than 16 percent of the snaps in Week 7, but he still handled nine touches for 71 yards and a score. The Commanders have only given up five rushing scores in six games, but they may struggle to contain Barkley, even if he’s at less than 100 percent. Stefon Diggs Anytime TD (+215) Stefon Diggs has four touchdown catches in five appearances in the 2026 season for the Commanders, and he’s now the No. 1 receiver with McLaurin done for the year. That’s led to 24 receptions for 214 yards, and Jayden Daniels has thrown the ball Diggs’ way a ton this season. In fact, Diggs found the end zone and had nine targets against this Philly team in Week 1. I’m buying him to have another big game on Sunday night, especially after he stepped up for six grabs and a score in Week 6. That workload should eventually turn into some scores, and this is a great matchup for the Eagles tight end to make it happen. Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee. The battle of the NFC East basement sees the Philadelphia Eagles visiting the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football. This division has been a mess in the first two months of the schedule, but Week 8 goes a long way to defining the second half of the schedule. My Eagles vs. Commanders predictions see SNF swinging in a different direction than the current markets would suggest, which is kind of on par with this upside-down division. Here are my favorite NFL picks for prime time on Nov. 1. TOP Pick Eagles vs Commanders prediction: Over 40.5 If you read my weekly NFL Underdogs column , you'll see I'm taking the points with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football. A big reason why is this underrated offense. Yes, Philadelphia has a backup under center and is potentially missing its top two WRs again. Yet, the Eagles have looked capable with Tanner McKee at the wheel. And with Saquon Barkley back, they went blow-for-blow with Dallas for 45 minutes on Monday until running out of ammo in the final frame. The Washington Commanders defense doesn't put up much of a fuss. Washington is a bottom-tier team in several key defensive measurements , including third-down conversions and red-zone defense. Making up for the soft stop unit is an offense that should at least be able to keep its quarterback clean. Philadelphia's once-vaunted pass rush is no more, boasting the fifth-lowest pressure rate , and that means Jayden Daniels has time in the pocket. Daniels is now four weeks returned from his elbow injury, with a bye in Week 7, and is coming off his best performance of the season. He passed for 300 yards and 72.5% completions with two TDs in a loss to San Francisco on Oct. 19. Eagles vs Commanders combo There's a lot of big-name firepower missing on both sides, but I see more meat on the bone for these offenses – especially considering that the complementing stop units are both garbage. Washington allowed Dallas Goedert to find the end zone twice in Week 1 and have given up the second most TDs to tight ends heading into Week 8. With the Eagles' receiving corps running thin, Goedert's role spikes on SNF. Rookie WR Antonio Williams is filling the void left by Terry McLaurin, doing plenty of damage out of the slot. He burned Philly in his NFL debut and is projected for as many as 46 receiving yards in Week 8. Goedert drew seven targets for five receptions in Week 7 and has been McKee's safety blanket during his two-game stint as the starter. The Eagles face a Commanders defense that has been bullied by rival tight ends this season. Washington ranks dead last in DVOA vs. tight ends, allowing the seventh most yards to the position along with eight touchdowns to TEs in just six games. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions in the Commanders' Showdown With the Eagles, Starting With Jayden Daniels - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders get their rematch with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night, and very little about it looks like the opener. Philadelphia won that one 24-22 when Washington's tying two-point try was stuffed. Since then, Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the season with blood clots in his lungs, and the Eagles have lost five straight, their longest skid since 2016. Washington (1-4-1) comes off its bye after a 23-17 loss in San Francisco that also cost it Terry McLaurin, who tore his patellar tendon and is done for the season, according to the team . Head coach Dan Quinn called the week off "a much-needed reset in a lot of ways," per the team's website . Philadelphia (2-5) lost 38-21 to Dallas on Monday night with Tanner McKee at quarterback. The Commanders are about a six-point favorite at Northwest Stadium and hold the EPA edge in nine of 12 categories. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday Night Football. Jayden Daniels leads Washington in rushing Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) is hit as he throws by San Francisco 49ers defensive end Romello Height (94) during the second quarter at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Daniels has 213 rushing yards on 25 carries, 8.5 per attempt, in four games, and his 88.7 rushing grade ranks third among quarterbacks, according to PFF . He has played the last two games in a brace after dislocating his left elbow in Week 2, and he ran only four times for 10 yards in San Francisco. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday. Washington needs him to run. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve with a groin injury , leaving Rachaad White (36 carries, 145 yards) as the lead back. Philadelphia ranks 27th against the run at 131.4 yards per game, and Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards against the Eagles on Monday. Bold prediction: Daniels runs for 75 yards and a touchdown, more than any Washington running back. Washington sacks Tanner McKee four times Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Washington Commanders linebacker Odafe Oweh (98) sacks Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) during the first quarter at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Quinn's defense blitzes more than any team except Minnesota, and it has only 11 sacks, tied for 22nd. "I'd love to see us, whether it's blitzing or rush coverage together, really being in sync with that," Quinn said Wednesday, per the team's website . Odafe Oweh leads the team with three sacks on 15 pressures, according to PFF , though he hasn't played up to his contract yet. K'Lavon Chaisson has 2.5 sacks and two forced fumbles. McKee is working behind a line that has allowed 18 sacks, and the Eagles had no sacks or quarterback hits of their own against Dallas. Bold prediction: Washington sacks McKee four times, even with Javon Kinlaw likely out with a knee injury. Antonio Williams beats Zack Baun this time Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams (14) makes a catch during the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Week 1 belonged to Zack Baun. Washington targeted him six times in coverage, and its pass catchers finished with minus-2 yards against him, per Next Gen Stats. He added 12 tackles and was named NFC Defensive Player of the Week . Baun is still fifth among linebackers with a 79.5 grade, but he has allowed a 100.0 passer rating in coverage, according to PFF . With McLaurin out, the rookie is the receiver Washington needs to change the equation . Antonio Williams has 18 catches for 205 yards and a touchdown, and he caught four passes for 64 yards and a score in the opener. Bold prediction: Williams goes over 75 yards, and at least one of those catches comes with Baun in coverage. Sonny Styles forces a turnover Sept. 27, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders linebacker Sonny Styles (52) gets the tackle and forces a fumble by Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price (8) in the first quarter at Northwest Stadium. Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Sonny Styles leads Washington with 46 tackles and has an interception, a sack and a forced fumble. He made 13 tackles in San Francisco, per NBC Washington , and his 72.7 coverage grade ranks 10th among linebackers, according to PFF . Philadelphia's offense ranks 29th in EPA, and Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks all missed practice Thursday, per the Eagles . That could leave McKee leaning on Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon over the middle, where Styles does his work. Washington is plus-6 in turnover differential, second in the NFL . Bold prediction: Styles forces a fumble or picks off McKee. The players on that defense know they were pushed around, and they know they weren't anywhere near good enough. It's not going to be the prettiest game – these two games have three wins in 13 combined games – but I think the Birds make just enough plays on defense to nose out the Commanders. away.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). away.headline: Eagles-Commanders Final Injury Report: Saquon Barkley WILL play
away.blurb: Barkley returned to practice on Friday — albeit in a limited capacity — after being listed under did not participate on Wednesday and Thursday. There’s no question that Barkley wanting to play and help his team try to turn the season around is admirable. But the team should protect him from himself and sit him down if he’s not nearly healthy enough to play and remain in the game. Which is reasonable to think that’s the case considering he wasn’t even able to fully participate in a practice this week! While overcompensating for his hamstring injury, Barkley injured his back on his first rushing attempt in Week 7 and then played sparingly through obvious discomfort the rest of the game. What’s the point of that? What if he gets further injured? That’s not only a setback as it relates to this season, which very well might be cooked anyway, but potentially long-term as well. It could also prevent teams from making offers not only ahead of the NFL trade deadline but in the offseason, too. Even if you’re not of the mind he should be traded at any point, you should want him healthy for next year! I just think playing him is a short-sighted decision with much more downside than upside. The Eagles ruled five players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Smith and Wicks did not practice this week ahead of their second straight game missed; the Eagles will once again be without their top two wide receivers. With Covey also out, the Eagles only have four healthy wide-outs on the roster: Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore. Against the Cowboys last week, Cooper played the most snaps of any Eagles WR while Lemon was right behind him. Despite this, Cooper only saw three targets while Lemon saw eight. The team will probably look to force-feed their rookie first-round pick again in this matchup. To be determined if they’ll look to elevate a fifth receiver from the practice squad. Their options there: Erik Ezukanma, Xavier Gipson (who also has returning experience), and Quentin Skinner. The Eagles ruled one player QUESTIONABLE: Jakorian Bennett. Bennett fully participated in practice all week. He’s still in his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday to activate him from IR in order for him to play on Sunday. They’ll need to open a roster spot to do so. Nolan Smith is notably set to return after missing Week 7 due to a concussion. Michael Carter II is also set to return after missing the Eagles’ last two games. Hunt and Ojomo will play but they were limited in practice all week. They’re clearly not 100%. On October 14, the Eagles opened Bennett’s 21-day practice window to return from IR. Bigsby is eligible to return to the roster after Week 8. Shipley is eligible to return to the roster after Week 9. Pierce is eligible to return to the roster after Week 12. Hurts, Sam and, Wilson are out for the season. Washington ruled one

home.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
home.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). home.blurb: Commanders receiver Treylon Burks was designated as questionable to play Sunday night's game against the Philadelphia Eagles due to a foot injury. That's especially notable for Washington's first game without Terry McLaurin, who suffered a season-ending torn patellar tendon against the 49ers in a Week 6 loss heading into a bye. Burks was among four Commanders listed as questionable on the official Commanders injury report, which was released on Friday. Tight end John Bates (shoulder), defensive lineman Johnny Newton (pectoral) — he's technically still on IR — and defensive tackle Daron Payne (foot) are also questionable. Defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw (knee) was ruled out of Sunday night's game, as expected. The Eagles will be without linebacker Jihad Campbell and receivers Davonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, though running back Saquon Barkley will be available. Barkley's status remains one of the biggest concerns after the veteran suffered a back injury during Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed him with hamstring and back injuries Wednesday, adding another concern for a player who recently returned from a hamstring issue that kept him out of consecutive games. Barkley opened the Dallas matchup with a 29-yard run and scored a touchdown on Philadelphia's first possession, but his workload was limited after his back tightened. He eventually left the game, forcing the Eagles to rely on their remaining running backs. Lemon responded with his first career touchdown reception against the Cowboys, but the Eagles would benefit from having additional receiving options available against Washington. Campbell was listed as a nonparticipant with hamstring and quadriceps injuries, adding to concerns for a defense that struggled against Dallas. Jones was sidelined by a hamstring injury, while Covey was listed with a knee injury after leaving Monday night's game. The defensive injury situation extends beyond those six players. Outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith were all listed as limited participants, along with defensive backs Michael Carter II, linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. The Eagles return to practice Thursday, and actual participation should better indicate which players are progressing toward Sunday's game. away.headline: Bears HC Ben Johnson shares injury update on Kyle Monangai
away.blurb: Johnson told the media that he isn't expecting Monangai to make his return to the field on Monday. "I would count him out this week," he said via Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune. Monangai has missed the last three games with a toe injury following a monster game against the New York Jets where he carried the ball 30 times for 146 yards and two rushing touchdowns in a 23-12 win. Though Monangai is not expected to play, Johnson is hopeful that tight end Colston Loveland will be good to go, according to Hammond. Loveland popped up on Friday's injury report with a neck injury, limiting him in practice. Johnson said the team is hopeful Loveland's injury is minor, but that they will need to see how he feels in practice on Saturday. Loveland is coming off his two best games of the season following the return of quarterback Caleb Williams to the lineup.
